📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Sources indicate that little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

Industry observers note that “It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick noted. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

According to recent reports, carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game plan.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

According to recent reports, mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick remarked. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick stated. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

Sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Sources indicate that dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

With City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Industry observers note that fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

It has been revealed that job done. Now a much bigger test awaits.

In a recent development, “Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another big one on Sunday.”.

Recent findings suggest that the final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

There will be three added minutes.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

How on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

In a recent development, sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

Perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

It has been revealed that dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

In a recent development, manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Industry observers note that mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

It has been revealed that is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

We are back under way at Old Trafford. How rapidly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

Sources indicate that that’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Half an hour in and United have been in command. It’s not scintillating but they warrant their lead and punished a misplaced pass by Parris brutally. Mainoo is orchestrating the game in the middle of the pitch. Best player on the park so far.

Industry observers note that parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

Tielemans steps in with a crucial interception inside his own box to deny Mickels the chance of a shot on goal.

The ball is then moved out to the left, where Dorgu crosses. He picks out Cunha, whose first-time effort with his side foot hits the Sabah keeper Pokatilov and goes into the net. Michael Carrick has made four changes for Sabah to the team that drew 2-2 against Everton. Benjamin Sesko is given his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford dropping to the bench. Luke Shaw was given an additional rest day on Wednesday and is left out of the squad. It makes sense with Sunday’s derby against Manchester City to come but it’s an early glimpse of the delicate balance Carrick will have to strike with his only recognised senior left back this season. Shaw can’t be expected to play every few days given his history of injury problems.

According to recent reports, it looks like Patrick Dorgu will be operating at left back against Sabah. This is United’s 300th fixture in the European Cup, including qualifiers. On the subject of qualifiers, Sabah became only the sixth side to navigate four qualifying rounds to reach the European Cup proper, with their campaign starting back on July 7. That was the same day Argentina beat Egypt in the last 16 of the World Cup. The Azerbaijan club were only formed nine years ago so have had quite the ascent since.

At 8pm on Thursday night, Manchester United will kick a ball in the Champions League for the first time in three seasons.

It must mark the start of a permanent return to Europe’s premier club competition. If United are serious about once again challenging for the Premier League title and building a £2bn stadium, that must be the way forward.

This is only the seventh time in 13 campaigns that United have been in the Champions League and the implications have been significant.

Presenting your Champions League Reds 📋❤️‍🔥.

Manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

It has been revealed that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

“It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

“I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the latest challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

In a recent development, sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (467 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.
  • Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:06 EST, 20 November 2026.

Tottenham star Tosin Adarabioyo has joined forces with former Chelsea team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill to launch a trading card shop in London.

Card Cop, opening in Borough Market on Thursday, will sell cards from a variety of sports as well as other collections such as Pokemon and Marvel.

According to recent reports, adarabioyo began collecting as a child and returned to the hobby in 2020. His collection, which he shares on social media, spans a variety of sports and he also has several of Brazilian icon Neymar.

'I’ve been collecting for years, and it’s great to see the hobby continue to grow,' said the 29-year-old, who left Chelsea for Spurs last summer.

'I love collecting. It’s a great way for supporters to connect with their favourite players. I’ve always felt that collectors are some of the most passionate fans.

Industry observers note that 'I’ve got to know so many collectors through the hobby. Talking about our collections is an instant icebreaker, and I know those conversations can mean a lot. I want to bring more players into the hobby and recreate those moments.

Tosin Adarabioyo, like many footballers, has a passion for collecting trading cards.

The new shop is set to open in London's Borough Market next week.

Adarabioyo enjoyes collecting cards of former PSG star Neymar, who won 130 caps for Brazil.

Industry observers note that 'Neymar is criminally underrated to me, and I think his cards are too. Some of the images take me straight back to performances I’ve watched over the years. It’s hard to describe, but it’s like bottling up that feeling forever. Football purists will know what I mean.'.

West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters, who played with Tosin at England youth level, is among backers along with James and Colwill.

Adarabioyo already has an online retail business, The Huddle, with guests such as Dominic Solanke, Robert Sanchez and Adam Wharton all featuring on live streams, opening boxes as fans watch.

Recent figures valued the global sports trading card market at $13.75billion (£10.5bn) in 2025, with that projected to grow to $27.52bn (£21bn) by 2034.

Formula One star Lewis Hamilton got in on the act earlier this year, launching his own venture and a shop in Frankfurt.

The seven-time world champion was already an ambassador for Topps - who also have the licence for Premier League cards - and noted: 'I’ve loved collecting cards since I was a kid — Pokemon, football, anything I could get my hands on.

Recent findings suggest that 'To now play a role in shaping the future of the category is incredible. We have a significant opportunity to tap into the culture in a way no one has before.'.

#152814. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4622 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4622 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

Hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he said.

“But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

Asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

In a recent development, “Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a big topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

This is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the issue yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Sources indicate that hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Industry observers note that defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury quickly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

According to recent reports, none of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also indicated quality and a threat. The joke is right now on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a latest reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I said to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

“Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

While his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Industry observers note that chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

Sources indicate that it was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

It has been revealed that we can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

Sources indicate that there have been 12 Premier League games at Anfield in 2026, Liverpool have only won 4 of them to date. This was seventh draw and Fulham deserves their share of the spoils. This was very much a learning experience for Andoni Iraola.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

Aston Villa 1 Nottingham Forest 2Bournemouth 2 Brentford 2Chelsea 2 Hull City 2Crystal Palace 2 Ipswich Town 3Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

What a result for Hull, who remain unbeaten and they have taken five points from fixtures against United, Villa and Chelsea.

That is the first really poor result of the Alonso era, points dropped.

What a thriller in SE25, both teams have been going for it in the closing stages, but Ipswich have surely score the winner through Zian Flemming.

Fulham were pointless before this game, but they have kept a clean sheet at Anfield with a disciplined display and they could well have score one or two. Underwhelming for Liverpool, who have not won just one of their first four games and their fixtures have not been the most taxing.

In a recent development, and as we predicted at the beginning of the game... Liverpool 0 Fulham 0. If this reporter ever gives you advice on a horse to back or a team to follow, make sure you take the opposite stance. Fulham deserve their reward and their fans are singing “We got a point!”.

Villa are finishing the game with 10 men because Ian Maatsen pulled up after Emery had made his five substitutions, and Forest have punished them through Igor Jesus with just a few minutes of normal time to play.

According to recent reports, alexander Isak heads over the bar when he perhaps should have hit the target. Has time run out for Liverpool?

Recent findings suggest that you might imagine Chelsea are battering down the door, but Mohamed-Ali Cho has just forced Emi Martinez into a save at the other end. Hull will remain unbeaten if they can hold out.

Strand Larsen has had his critics, but he has scored his first goal of the season to set up a grandstand finish with 15 minutes plus stoppage time to play at Selhurst Park.

Short corner, McGinn whipped in an inswinging cross that is glanced into the bottom corner by Alysson.

Liverpool continue to toil at Anfield, but no opening goal. Iraola has thrown on Frimpong, Mac Allister, Ngumoha and Gakpo in the second half. Fulham have had the chances to score at least one, and Josh King has just brought a save out of Alisson.

Hull are a little lucky they still have 11 men on the pitch. Already on a booking, my man Crooks bundled down Rogers. It could easily have been another yellow car but the referee let him off and now he’s been replaced by Iroegbunam.

Joao Pedro finds the smallest of gaps to be the goalkeeper and find the roof of the net with a brilliant, instinctive finish.

In a recent development, that had not really been coming for Chelsea. It all felt a bit easy for Palmer to get his low cross into the box and Pedro to sweep the ball in. The home fans have woken up again.

According to recent reports, martinez was lucky to get away with another slip up, there. He spilt Slater’s shot but reacted before McBurnie to stop the Hull striker scoring the rebound. Just a day after his nasty looking crash, Sorba Thomas is on for Hull.

This game is absolutely here for Fulham to win. Quietness has descended around Anfield, the hosts have no fluency in their play and Fulham are growing in confidence. Why wouldn’t they after getting to 65 minutes with a clean sheet?

Industry observers note that just like in the first half, four minutes after one of these teams taking the lead there has been an equaliser. Kevin Scahde is in a rich vein of form.

It has been revealed that bournemouth have have never beaten Brentford in the Premier League, but they might well be on their way to changing that record having trailed earlier in the game. Marcus Tavernier has just scored their second goal.

It has been revealed that matt Davidson Rider Crooks has just been booked for a very cynical foul on Rogers. It gave Chelsea a free-kick in a dangerous position Reece James had an effort tipped away. Chelsea have started the second half well.

Within a minute of the restart, Villa lose the ball in midfield and Delap punishes them to the maximum. Cracking finish from just outside the box, and a much-needed goal by Delap. The Glasner curse striking for Emery again?

Liam Delap has just started paying back that £50m transfer fee with a fine goal.

Delap picked the ball up on the left and set himself up on the edge of the box before crashing a 25-yard shot past Zion Suzuki.

Unai Emery has made a couple of changes at half-time, taking off Nicolas Jackson who picked up a silly booking just before half-time.

In a recent development, tammy Abraham is on in his place. George Hemmings is also off and replaced by Alysson.

Recent findings suggest that pep Chavarria on for Chelsea at half-time. He’s replaced Jorrel Hato, who had a bit of a stinker in the first half.

It has been revealed that andoni Iraola hasn’t hung about here. Milos Kerkez has come on immediately after half-time for Kostas Tsimikas and you can say with certainty that Liverpool will be shopping for a newly introduced left-back in due course.

Industry observers note that so at half-time, Hull City are top of the Premier League and don’t their supporters know it? They were singing “we are top of the League” for the full two minutes of time added on for stoppages at the end of the first period. Alonso has some work to do at the break.

Forest did need a brilliant double save from Matz Sels to deny Victor Lindelof and have recovered to slow the match down.

Neco Williams wasted a decent chance for Forest from outside the penalty area shortly before the break.

Referee Andrew Madley has irritated both teams with a number of weird decisions - but that’s sadly par for the course with officials nowadays.

Villa 0 Forest 0Bournemouth 1 Brentford 1Chelsea 1 Hull City 2Palace 1 Ipswich 2Liverpool 0 Fulham 0.

Palace in some trouble now, level with Ipswich and down to 10 men. Disasi was sent off in the 34th minute for a reckless challenge on Jack Clarke, caught him with studs on shin.

Things got worse for Palace just before half-time, with Leif Davis heading home at the back post to give Ipswich the league.

Sources indicate that apologies for the lack of updates, some technical gremlins at Telegraph Towers. A nip and tuck game as expected at at the Vitality: Kevin Schade gave Brentford the lead before Justin Kluivert equalised four minutes later.

One way to put it is that Kostas Tsimikas isn’t playing well. Another way to say it would be that his efforts are making Milos Kerkez look like Roberto Carlos. The Greek left-back is having a dreadful afternoon and Fulham are getting plenty of joy out of him. We suggested there was no chance of this game finishing goalless, and it’s anomalous that we have reached 40 minutes without score. Fulham, certainly, have a sense of adventure and have been into Liverpool’s 18-yard box plenty of times. Let’s see if the picture changes before the interval.

It has been revealed that that’s now seven goals Emi Martinez has conceded in three games since joining from Villa to supposedly solve Chelsea’s goalkeeping crisis. Martinez won’t be pleased with Hull’s second goal, here. He was beaten to a corner by Ajayi. His header hit the bar and Belloumi’s shot was deflected past him. The Hull fans are in dreamland.

This is a turn up for the books. Chelsea undone by a long ball forward, and Hato lets the ball bounce over his head, and Belloumi finishes with aplomb.

That’s now 20 Premier League games Chelsea have gone without keeping a clean sheet. What an earth was Jorrel Hato doing, letting the ball bounce over him for Belloumi? Amateur stuff at the back from the home side. It was Hull’s first meaningful attack.

Emersonn has struggled in some games so far this season, but he has just planted a header into the corner from a Davis cross.

According to recent reports, there is a VAR check for offside... but the goal stands.

According to recent reports, 5 - Morgan Rogers is the fifth different player to score or assist in each of Chelsea's first four games of a Premier League season, after Didier Drogba (2010-11), Cesc Fàbregas (2014-15), Diego Costa (2014-15 & 2016-17), and Eden Hazard (2018-19).Famous. pic.twitter.com/0cuThzH472.

In a recent development, A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Recent findings suggest that austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

Sources indicate that an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

According to recent reports, wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez launched the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

We’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

Industry observers note that although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

Recent findings suggest that we are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a massive buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

Sources indicate that will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ.

I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

According to recent reports, hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

Recent findings suggest that we know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a big game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a latest chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures new in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

Liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and upcoming manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

It has been revealed that chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Sources indicate that glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Recent findings suggest that the Blues are 4th in the Championship table despite Saturday’s loss, but the result wasn’t the only dampener on a tricky day at the office.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, birmingham City saw their impressive form halted on Saturday as they lost 1-0 away at fellow high-flyers Stoke City. It was a frustrating day for BCFC, but recent evidence suggests they’re well placed to return to winning ways when they face Burnley on Wednesday night.

Recent findings suggest that the Blues are 4th in the Championship table despite Saturday’s loss, but the result wasn’t the only dampener on a tricky day at the office. Club captain and standout defender Christoph Klarer was booked in the first half, and as it was his fifth yellow card of the campaign, he now faces a one-match suspension.

Birmingham City aren’t blessed with strength in numbers at centrre-back, but in rarely-seen summer signing Dael Fry, Chris Davies has a fine player to call upon to cover for the absence of star man Klarer.

Recent findings suggest that fry has been a Championship mainstay for almost his entire career. He came through the academy of hometown club Middlesbrough and barring a stint on loan at Rotherham United, he had spent his full playing career at the Riverside Stadium.

Industry observers note that he marked a strong free transfer signing for Birmingham City in the summer. However, after 16 games of the Championship campaign, Fry has made just two substitute appearances, totalling only two minutes. On both occasions, he came on off the bench to help see out 2-1 victories – first over Wrexham, and then Derby County.

Fry has been unused on the BCFC bench on 12 occasions, but as the only other centre-back alongside regular starters Klarer and Phil Neumann, the 29-year-old is bound to come into the team at Burnley.

Industry observers note that losing Klarer is far from ideal, but Fry is a fine replacement. Wednesday night will bring his 275th Championship appearance, and he offers a strong aerial presence at the back while thriving in duels and one-on-one defending. He can be trusted in possession as well, so should slot into Davies’ defence with ease.

Upon swapping Middlesbrough for Birmingham City, Fry will have hoped for more minutes than he has found. Klarer and Neumann have been an unbreakable partnership though, forcing the summer signing to watch on from the bench more often than not.

Sources indicate that given his status as a Championship stalwart, that will have frustrated the former Boro ace. But, Fry’s influence will have been felt through his leadership and professionalism, offering a strong presence in the dressing room and on the training ground.

This clash with Burnley offers a welcome chance for Fry to show BCFC fans that he is more than ready to deliver when called upon, despite the fact he is a clear third-choice central defender at St Andrew’s.

Liverpool games v Man United and Everton moved as Premier League confirm updated fixture details

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.
  • With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.
  • The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Two more Liverpool fixtures in the Premier League have been rescheduled for live TV coverage, as confirmed on Thursday.

With the November international break now concluded, the Reds’ next couple of domestic fixtures are against Manchester United and Everton, with the reverse of those games against our two biggest traditional rivals taking place on consecutive weekends in January.

The fixture list for the remainder of this year had already been locked in, and the first month of 2027 has now been set, other than prospective FA Cup and Carabao Cup matches.

On Thursday, the Premier League announced updated dates and times for matches in January, with two of Liverpool’s games being moved.

The home clash against Crystal Palace remains a 3pm kick-off on Saturday 16th, but the subsequent two games have unsurprisingly been chosen for TV coverage.

The Reds will now face Manchester United at Old Trafford on Sunday 24 January at 4:30pm (live on Sky Sports), with the Merseyside derby at Anfield taking place six days later with a 12:30pm kick-off (live on TNT Sports).

Recent findings suggest that want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust.

The newly introduced dates and times for the Man United and Everton games have left Liverpool with a rather difficult week towards the end of January.

Just three days after the game at Old Trafford, the Reds have their concluding fixture in the league phase of the Champions League at home to Lens, and then a turnaround of just over 50 hours to hosting the Toffees at Anfield.

*FA Cup third round draw and fixture details to be confirmed in December.

**If Liverpool advance to Carabao Cup semi-finals.

The hope is that, by the time the Ligue 1 outfit visit L4 on 27 January, we’ll already be assured of a direct passage to the round of 16 and there won’t be anything riding on that game for Andoni Iraola’s side.

Liverpool right now have seven matches in the diary in the first month of 2027, with an FA Cup third-round tie to be added for the weekend of 9/10 January and a potential Carabao Cup semi-final first leg in the subsequent midweek, should we defeat Bournemouth at Anfield next month.

It’s quite plausible that the Reds could have two matches against Everton in January, with both teams still in the Carabao Cup and favourites to win their respective quarter-finals (the Toffees are away to Fleetwood of League Two).

Three Merseyside derbies in the first five weeks of 2027 would be the definition of familiarity breeding contempt, but for now the sole focus for Iraola and co is the small matter of Man United at home on Sunday.

Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3429 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open latest opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

In a recent development, a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

Recent findings suggest that a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

Industry observers note that a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

In a recent development, a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

Recent findings suggest that a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

According to recent reports, a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that west Brom made it seven Championship games without defeat on Saturday as they drew 2-2 with Swansea City away from home.
  • According to recent reports, after Rabby Nzingoula put the Baggies 2-1 up, Jayson Molumby was fouled from a set piece and the visitors were given a penalty.
  • The fluffed attempt was swiftly followed by Elijah Just’s equaliser, and it prompted serious frustration towards Price.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that west Brom made it seven Championship games without defeat on Saturday as they drew 2-2 with Swansea City away from home. WBA went ahead on two occasions and were pegged back both times, but the most frustrating part of the tie was that they missed a gilt-edged chance to go 3-1 up.

According to recent reports, after Rabby Nzingoula put the Baggies 2-1 up, Jayson Molumby was fouled from a set piece and the visitors were given a penalty. Isaac Price, who tapped home the opener, stepped up and saw his panenka attempt saved by Swans’ shot-stopper Lawrence Vigouroux.

The fluffed attempt was swiftly followed by Elijah Just’s equaliser, and it prompted serious frustration towards Price. It proved to be a costly moment, but West Brom can rely on their star man to bounce back.

Sources indicate that price’s development has been fascinating to watch since joining West Brom. He played almost entirely in central positions in his youth career at Everton and he stayed there while at Standard Liege for the most part, occasionally filling in as a right wing-back.

Recent findings suggest that however, since joining West Brom, Price has become a true goalscoring attacking midfielder. He initially played in a central role as a No. 10, but in 2026 he has locked down a place on the left wing, and the 23-year-old has become a dependable goal threat.

According to recent reports, not only that, but the level of confidence Price is playing with for Albion has brought flair to his game. He isn’t opposed to taking on his man with quick footwork, improvising with a flick, or attempting a panenka penalty.

The WBA star produced a brilliantly executed chipped spot-kick against Blackburn Rovers. Some may argue that it was foolish of Price to attempt another just weeks later, and they’d be right in hindsight. However, the audacity to try back-to-back panenka penalties is part of being a flair player, and it emphasises the freedom and confidence he is playing with.

Was that confidence misplaced on Saturday? Perhaps. But if it had come off, there’s no doubt that Albion fans and pundits alike would be lauding the cheek of Price for pulling off such a finish once again.

Price will be determined to bounce back from Saturday’s penalty miss, and there’s no reason to doubt that he can. The West Brom star has been in fantastic form this season, and he has arguably become one of their most crucial players.

Sources indicate that despite the miss, Price now has three goals and an assist in his last three Championship games. He can be trusted to deliver goals from the left-hand side and plays a crucial role in build-up play, as his technical ability from his previous time as a central midfielder helps him play incisive passes and maintain control of the ball.

WBA face Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday night, and Price can produce an instant response to his Swansea City mishap. The Trotters play on the front foot and there will be gaps in behind for the Baggies’ attackers to exploit.

Price will likely match up against right-back Luca Stephenson, who is a dependable and energetic player. He has been booked four times in seven games though, so he could be worth targeting in one-on-ones.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:32 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 20 November 2026.

Jack Grealish has been offered an olive branch by Everton boss David Moyes and mentioned the sanctioned star is available for selection this weekend.

Industry observers note that the Manchester City loanee was punished by the club for failing to report to training sessions and missed several matches. He has not featured for four games: one because of illness, then a ‘breach of club discipline’ and a lack of fitness thereafter.

But Grealish will be considered for the squad when the in-form Toffees travel to Brentford on Monday night.

Moyes said: ‘He has served his punishment and we will treat him as we were treating him before.

In a recent development, ‘We will get on with things. The team is going really well at the moment and what I don’t want to do is turn it into a Jack story because it shouldn’t be.’.

Pushed if that suggests he will not play on Monday night, Moyes replied: ‘He could easily. He is back in the squad, he is a good player. Who knows?’.

Jack Grealish is available for Everton again after serving his punishment and regaining fitness.

Everton have won their last three games and go into Monday’s match sixth in the table.

Asked what Grealish can offer, the boss added: ‘Jack can offer us a lot. I want more from him, I want him to show more than he has done. I want him to give me more assists, goals.

‘But there's lots of things about him which we need and he's good at retaining the ball, giving us good possession, carrying. So we hope that he can get back to those levels and give us what we need.

‘I think this time last year he was probably sitting on five or six assists so we're hoping to get that.’.

Grealish's social media apology came after he featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break.

'Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training!' Grealish wrote. 'I want to apologise to the fans (and) everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

A presentation from Blues past and present. 🤝Leon Osman and James Tarkowski surprise David Moyes with a memento as he sets a new record for games managed for Everton Football Club (593). 💙 pic.twitter.com/tzFuGeUhFW.

'I love playing for this club (and) can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt.

'See you all soon (blue heart)'.

At the start of his press conference Moyes was presented with a framed memento of his time in charge by defender James Tarkowski and former player Leon Osman after he set a new club record of 593 games in the hotseat.

Moyes noted: 'It’s something that I’m really thrilled about but, if I’m being honest, it’s not something I really think about. I understand I’ve suddenly become the manager who’s had more games at Everton than anybody before and that’s a real honour and privilege to be put in that position.'.
