#152781. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 20m • 📚 Deep Dive (4099 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

£329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4099 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.
  • A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he stated. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

Spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

It has been revealed that at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

In a recent development, “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

In a recent development, spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

In a recent development, some surprised faces then when Moyes stated later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

It has been revealed that the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes stated that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Industry observers note that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

Industry observers note that de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He remarked that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

Recent findings suggest that “We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender mentioned: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and indicated that mentality again in the second half.

According to recent reports, “We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

According to recent reports, "Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young says that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx.

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev.

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

Dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

Industry observers note that there will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Recent findings suggest that pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6.

Sources indicate that tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

In a recent development, garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

Spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a major chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Industry observers note that johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t.

According to recent reports, everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

It has been revealed that antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Recent findings suggest that following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

The start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors presently have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

George does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

According to recent reports, spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

Industry observers note that we are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

Industry observers note that an uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

It has been revealed that there will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

Recent findings suggest that there has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

Recent findings suggest that that is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

It has been revealed that tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

Gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Major question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

Tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

In a recent development, greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Recent findings suggest that everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

"Solanke is a crucial player"Roberto De Zerbi on the importance of Dominic Solanke being fit for Spurs 💪 pic.twitter.com/FNWNsTWdt8.

Ready to go 🔋 pic.twitter.com/dFb8UyiZOl.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

Industry observers note that “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” indicates Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

Sources indicate that “I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

🎧🫡 Thierno Barry ahead of today's clash in North London. pic.twitter.com/mwlsKH8Pid.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

After scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Today's Toffees to face @SpursOfficial. COYB! ✊#TOTEVE pic.twitter.com/mOcCayRUfm.

In a recent development, roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

In a recent development, this game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

Sources indicate that alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

Tech Report: Michael Duff admits substantial selection ‘risk’ that paid off in Bradford City’s draw with Doncaster Rovers

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (685 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that bradford City man Nick Powell has had an injury-plagued career and has opened up about how he considered retiring last January due to his constant setbacks.
  • On Saturday, Powell secured his first league start of the season and repaid Michael Duff‘s faith by scoring the opening goal in a 2-2 draw with Yorkshire rivals Doncaster Rovers.
  • The Bantams saw three points snatched from them after a 95th-minute equaliser by Sean Grehan.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that bradford City man Nick Powell has had an injury-plagued career and has opened up about how he considered retiring last January due to his constant setbacks. But the former Manchester United midfielder has stayed fit this season, and is reaping the rewards for his availability.

On Saturday, Powell secured his first league start of the season and repaid Michael Duff‘s faith by scoring the opening goal in a 2-2 draw with Yorkshire rivals Doncaster Rovers.

The Bantams saw three points snatched from them after a 95th-minute equaliser by Sean Grehan. Despite the disappointing end to the clash, there were positives to take for the hosts, with Powell’s performance and start being one of them.

Recent findings suggest that bradford City boss Duff spoke highly of Powell post-match, acknowledging that it was a risk to start him before highlighting his importance to the side. As quoted by the Yorkshire Post, he said:.

It has been revealed that “It was his first league start (this season), and he’s been here a long time. It was always a risk. There are lengthy conversations from a psychological and a physical point of view, which him, the physios, the sports scientists and myself are all involved in, because he can do things that other players at this level can’t.

Sources indicate that “Nick’s missed a lot of football in his career and he’s now in his later years and it looks like he’s enjoying being out on the pitch. The only reason he’s played at this level is because of his body, his injury history. He’s influential in the group. They look up to him because none of our other players and staff have ever been at Man United.”.

The midfielder-turned-striker has found his feet this season at Valley Parade and is growing in confidence, week by week. His injury record has hampered his chances of breaking into the City starting squad sooner, but right now, the No. 9 spot is his to lose.

The 32-year-old is in a rich vein of form right now, scoring four and assisting one in his last three appearances.

According to recent reports, nobody has ever doubted Powell’s ability on a football pitch, whether that was him playing in the Premier League or when he was playing in League Two. But, the one thing that has held him back in his career is injuries.

Right now though, the Crewe-born man has strung a healthy run of games together, and to go with that, plenty of positive performances too.

Sources indicate that powell’s manager and Bradford City teammates all speak so highly of him and how vital he is to the squad both on and off the pitch. His wealth of experience playing in higher divisions is crucial for the Bantams as they look to secure promotion to the Championship this season.

Recent findings suggest that if Powell can continue his great run of form and maintain his availability during the busiest period of the season, then he will only grow in confidence regarding his body. Even though we are only in November, he has already played in more games this season than in any of the previous two campaigns in the league, with 12 appearances.

According to recent reports, the Bantams are in a tricky spot right now when it comes to league form, having won just one of their last seven. But Powell has been a shining light for Bradford in what has been a difficult run of results.

Key QPR man set to miss Norwich City trip as 26-year-old nears return

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (589 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, QPR defeated Millwall on Saturday, winning 1-0 through a first-half goal from the returning Nicolas Madsen.
  • Industry observers note that the Hoops make the quick turnaround to face Norwich City on Tuesday, and manager Julien Stephan has admitted skipper Dunne is unlikely to return for the Carrow Road trip.
  • In better news for QPR, full-back Tariq Lamptey has returned to training and is likely to be available despite also missing the Millwall win.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, QPR defeated Millwall on Saturday, winning 1-0 through a first-half goal from the returning Nicolas Madsen. However, one man who sat out was captain Jimmy Dunne, who picked up an ankle injury while away with the Republic of Ireland over the international break.

Industry observers note that the Hoops make the quick turnaround to face Norwich City on Tuesday, and manager Julien Stephan has admitted skipper Dunne is unlikely to return for the Carrow Road trip. As quoted by West London Sport, he remarked: “Not definitely, but probably not. It’s not a bad one. I don’t know exactly when he will be able to come back. He is still in a little bit of pain, so let’s see in the next days how the situation evolves.”.

In better news for QPR, full-back Tariq Lamptey has returned to training and is likely to be available despite also missing the Millwall win. The 26-year-old has been out with an ankle issue and last played in the 1-1 draw away at West Ham on October 9th.

In a recent development, stephan has not been afraid to make changes and he is expected to shuffle the ranks for the trip to Norwich City on Tuesday night. Despite Dunne’s absence, he does still have room to make a change at centre-back if he wishes.

Ronnie Edwards captained QPR in the Millwall triumph, and he was partnered by Jake Clarke-Salter at centre-back on their way to a welcome clean sheet. The former Chelsea prospect will be the favourite to partner the stand-in skipper as a result.

It has been revealed that but, if he wishes to make a switch, Stephan will have Liam Morrison to call upon. The 23-year-old is yet to make a competitive appearance this season and has been an unused substitute for 10 of the last 11 Championship matches.

It has been revealed that if one of the centre-backs was to drop out, it would likely be Clarke-Salter in order to manage his minutes. The 29-year-old has had injury problems over recent seasons but he has only missed two league matchday squads this term.

QPR don’t have the biggest senior squad in the Championship with 26 first-team players. However, they are well stocked in all areas and have already dealt with injuries this term, mainly in attack.

It has been revealed that stephan has shown a willingness to dip into the academy when needed as well. Leon Scarlett has emerged in the senior group, and 20-year-old midfielder Isak Alemayehu has appeared in matchday squads fairly regularly as well.

The Hoops have built the squad well over the past 18 months or so. The summer window saw them boost revamp their options at full-back and in goal, and there’s a balanced and well-rounded squad at Stephan’s disposal as a result.

It means he has room to make changes and ample cover when injuries hit.

Latest Update: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 28 min read (5527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder demonstrates near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate–forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

It has been revealed that symbols indicate data sources, including sites with (1) both eddy-covariance flux and phenocam observations (n = 3; green stars); (2) eddy-covariance flux only (n = 1; blue star); (3) phenocam observations only (n = 2; yellow stars); (4) litterfall observations (n = 47; red triangles); (5) inventory plots (n = 289; purple circles); and (6) very high-resolution Google Earth image locations (n = 16; 0.5-m spatial resolution, each covering a 2 km × 2 km area; blue squares). Site information, including location, data type, and observation period, is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The map was created using ArcGIS Pro with the Esri World Ocean Base basemap. Basemap sources: Esri, Garmin, GEBCO, NOAA NGDC and other contributors.

In a recent development, panels a-e compare the temporal dynamics of ecosystem-scale deciduousness fraction from Sentinel-2 (blue line) with the fraction of leafless tree crowns visually assessed from phenocam images (black line). The Sentinel-2 deciduousness fraction is calculated as the mean value within a 500 m × 500 m area centred on each phenocam site, while the phenocam typically covers an area of approximately 100 m × 100 m. Panel f indicates the relationship between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness and the corresponding deciduousness derived from phenocam observations across five sites (n = 60 paired site-month observations). The solid line indicates an ordinary least-squares linear regression, with statistical significance assessed using a two-sided test (p = 6.17 × 10−22).

In a recent development, a, Relationship between standardized monthly litterfall and standardized satellite-derived deciduousness across annual cycles at 47 Amazonian sites (n = 559 pooled site-month observations). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear regression across all pooled data, and the inset boxplot summarizes the site-level distribution of correlation coefficients (r, n = 47 sites). b, Relationship between satellite-derived deciduousness amplitude and the ground-derived proportion of deciduous tree species across the Amazon basin. Grey circles represent raw plot-to-pixel observations (n = 289 plots). The red line indicates the ordinary least-squares linear fit to the raw observations, and the shaded band indicates the 95% confidence interval of the fitted mean relationship. The dashed grey line indicates the 1:1 relationship. For a and b, statistical significance of the regression slopes was assessed using two-sided tests (a, p = 2.52 × 10−141; b, p = 7.24 × 10−28). The p values were not adjusted for multiple comparisons. c, Patch-level comparison of deciduousness derived from Sentinel-2 (y-axis) against that derived from closely date-matched, high-resolution Google Earth imagery (GEI; x-axis) via image-specific Random Forest classification and pooled across all 16 validation scenes. Each dot represents a 100-m × 100-m aggregated patch (n = 6058 patches), and the dashed black line marks the 1:1 relationship. d, e, Scene-level distributions of correlation coefficients (r; d) and root-mean-square errors (RMSE; e) calculated separately for each of the 16 GEI validation scenes. Grey dots represent individual scenes. In all boxplots, the centre line indicates the median, the box bounds the interquartile range (IQR), and the whiskers extend to 1.5 × IQR.

a, c, e, g, Spatial maps of evergreen forest cover (a), MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields tree cover (c), EVI amplitude (e) and VOD amplitude (g). Inset histograms show the basin-wide frequency distribution of each metric. b, d, f, h, Corresponding pixel-level relationships between Sentinel-2-derived deciduousness amplitude and the four reference metrics. Hexbin colour indicates observation density, and dashed lines indicate least-squares linear regressions. Sample sizes (b, d, f, h) were n = 227,612, 227,612, 226,942 and 221,884 valid paired forest pixels, reflecting product-specific data availability. All two-sided tests gave p < 10−300. Correlation coefficients (r) and regression equations are shown in each panel.

Panels a-h show how each variable affects deciduousness–greenness asynchrony, with positive SHAP values (>0) indicating a positive effect and negative SHAP values (<0) indicating a negative effect. The black line in each panel represents a fitted line, summarizing the central tendency of the data points.

Bar charts show the proportional influence of hydroclimate, soil, and light for the entire basin (a), Southern Amazon (b), Guiana Shield (c), and Everwet Amazon (d).

Industry observers note that a-c, Spatial patterns of model-performance gain, expressed as the change in the correlation coefficient (Δr) between the GPP seasonality simulated by LD-LUE and that simulated by each corresponding conventional LUE model, with both evaluated against satellite SIF. Results are shown for the EC-LUE (a), two-leaf EC-LUE (TL-EC-LUE; b) and MODIS-LUE (c). Positive Δr indicates better agreement of LD-LUE with satellite SIF relative to its conventional counterpart. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0.

Industry observers note that a-l, Comparisons of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites (K34, K67, CAX, and RJA). Rows correspond to the three core LUE formulations: EC-LUE (a-d), TL-EC-LUE (e-h), and MODIS-LUE (i–l). Black dashed lines with open circles represent EC observations. Coloured lines with open markers represent conventional baselines driven by various vegetation inputs (e.g., NDVI, EVI, kNDVI, MODIS-LAI), whereas solid red lines with filled markers denote the LD-LUE models. m, n, Dumbbell plots showing site-level performance and across-site mean in terms of the temporal correlation coefficient (r) (m) and RMSE (n). Open symbols denote the conventional baselines, whereas the corresponding filled symbols denote the LD-LUE models. The vertical lines connecting each pair indicate the magnitude and direction of performance changes following incorporation of the LD module. Symbol colours distinguish the baseline input configurations, and symbol shapes indicate the underlying model formulations (circles, EC-LUE; triangles, TL-EC-LUE; squares, MODIS-LUE).

a-d, Spatial distribution of model performance gain, expressed as Δr, for EC-LUE (a), TL-EC-LUE (b), MODIS-LUE (c), and mean Δr across the three models (d). Δr is calculated as the difference in the correlation coefficient between satellite SIF and the GPP seasonality simulated by the LD-LUE model (that incorporates both satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs and leaf demography) and that simulated by the corresponding baseline model (which includes only satellite deciduousness-constrained structural inputs). Positive values indicate improved seasonal agreement with SIF after incorporating leaf-age-dependent physiological dynamics, whereas negative values indicate reduced agreement. Insets show the basin-wide distributions of Δr, with the red dashed line marking Δr = 0 and the annotated values indicating the percentage of forest pixels with Δr > 0. e, Stacked bar chart showing the proportional breakdown of pixels with improved (red) and degraded (blue) Δr averaged across the three models, for each ecoregion (Southern Amazon, Guiana Shield, and Everwet Amazon) and the entire Amazon basin.

a-d, Comparison of monthly GPP seasonality at four Amazonian EC flux-tower sites: K34 (a), K67 (b), CAX (c), and RJA (d). Red lines with triangles represent the full leaf-demography-enabled model (LD-LUE), while blue lines with squares represent the baseline model (LAIdec-LUE), which uses the same deciduousness-derived LAI but assumes a seasonally fixed photosynthetic capacity. Black dashed lines with open circles indicate the EC-derived GPP observations. Shaded bands indicate ±1 standard error of the mean (SEM; n = 3 LUE formulations per ensemble). e-g, Quantitative assessment of model performance gains across the four sites, comparing LD-LUE (red bars) and LAIdec-LUE (blue bars) in terms of correlation coefficient (r; e), root mean square error (RMSE; f), and amplitude ratio (g). The amplitude ratio in (g) is calculated relative to the observed seasonal amplitude, with the horizontal dashed line at 1.0 indicating perfect agreement.

Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4558 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands.
  • Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality.
  • So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o.

According to recent reports, the former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he stated. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

According to recent reports, other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Another start for the Arsenal midfielder, another 90 minutes completed and another performance of constructive passing and destructive defending. For anyone who was worried about Rice’s physical condition, it was an emphatic response.

After that Champions League victory over Napoli, Rice insisted he was ready for another marathon campaign. He made 69 appearances for club and country last season, up from 60 the previous term, and believes that is a sustainable number of games, even for an all-action midfielder such as himself. “I have shown I can do it,” he mentioned.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. There is no doubt that his body eventually began to pay the price for his exertions last year, especially during the World Cup, and it would be reasonable for his managers to worry that his extraordinary workload might one day take a serious toll.   • Lawlor has drawn high praise for his work with the Seasiders’ North West coast neighbours, where he has been in permanent charge since March.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that blackpool sacked Ian Evatt last week, leaving the Tangerines on the lookout for a new boss. They were defeated in their first game under Steve Thompson’s interim lead, losing to fellow strugglers Wigan Athletic 2-1 at home.

Now, a newly introduced name has been linked with the vacancy at Bloomfield Road. According to reporter Pete O’Rourke, one man under consideration for the job at Blackpool is Fleetwood Town boss Matt Lawlor.

Lawlor has drawn high praise for his work with the Seasiders’ North West coast neighbours, where he has been in permanent charge since March. The 38-year-old is under contract with Fleetwood until the summer of 2028 at present, so a compensation fee would be required to bring him in as Evatt’s replacement.

Born in Poulton-le-Fylde, Lawlor is a North West native. He played for Blackpool’s youth academy as a youngster before going on to play non-league football with Farsley Celtic, AFC Fylde and Bamber Bridge.

He coached alongside his playing career from a young age, working with Manchester United before joining the Fleetwood Town setup in 2019. Lawlor held various roles in their academy and spent a few spells at their sister club Waterford FC, serving as assistant manager once and caretaker boss twice.

Sources indicate that an impressive stint as temporary boss of the Cod Army in January 2026 saw Lawlor given his maiden full-time gig in senior football, and he has made a good impression. He isn’t blessed with resources at Highbury Stadium, but he’s delivered respectable results through fine match preparation and some smart in-game coaching, as shown by the shock Carabao Cup win over Premier League champions Arsenal.

Lawlor’s future at Fleetwood is secure with a contract until 2028, but that might not be enough to fend off interest from elsewhere.

Industry observers note that lawlor’s good work at Fleetwood Town means interest from Blackpool is more than justified. It could prove a tempting opportunity too.

Recent findings suggest that geographically, he could make the step up to League One without having to move away from home. His past as a youth player at Bloomfield Road could mean there are sentimental temptations as well.

In a recent development, that mentioned, it does feel as though Lawlor is in a good place right now. After various roles in the Fishermen’s setup and at Waterford, he has developed well. He’s still only 38 and in the formative years of his time as a first-team boss too, so may be wary of making the step up too early.

Time will tell whether the rumoured interest comes to anything, with Blackpool sure to be considering plenty of contenders.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026.
  • Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.
  • According to recent reports, it was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 11:24 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 18:21 EST, 20 November 2026.

Chelsea have been slapped with a significant £150,000 fine by the Football Association for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic more than ten months ago.

According to recent reports, it was alleged that in the 56th minute, the visiting supporters at the Valley sang ‘f*** the Pope and the IRA’. A charge followed, and Chelsea were hit with their fine, along with being given an action strategy to follow and a formal warning as to their future conduct.

Industry observers note that chelsea tried to appeal being fined £150,000 for the sectarian chanting. They wanted it either removed completely, or at least substantially reduced.

The club attempted to argue that it was excessive despite admitting that approximately 2,500 of their fans may have taken part in the offensive singing. They also noted how Millwall were previously not fined for the same chant occurring.

Their appeal was dismissed and the full scale of their punishment was upheld.

Recent findings suggest that in a statement, Chelsea noted of the chanting: ‘We unequivocally condemn this behaviour. Sectarian abuse – chanting that creates division targeted towards a particular religious or political group – and discriminatory language of any kind has no place in our football club.

Chelsea have been hit with a £150,000 fine for their fans’ behaviour during an FA Cup away tie at Charlton Athletic back in January.

Xabi Alonso insists his Chelsea stars will show they are not 'soft' after Leeds United rubbed in how often they have bullied their opponents in a video uploaded to their social media.

Leeds produced a compilation of clips of their players leaving crunching challenges in on their Chelsea counterparts and capitalising on mistakes made down the years.

In a recent development, daniel Farke's side have won more duels than any other club in the Premier League this season, and Alonso's team crumbled when visiting Sunderland before the international break. That was a game in which Levi Colwill and Co were bullied by Brian Brobbey. Colwill was hooked at half-time in that 1-0 loss at the Stadium of Light.

Dominic Calvert-Lewin may now be relishing testing Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, but Alonso remarked when asked about being seen as weak: 'We focus on not being soft and being competitive. That's our goal. We have played once this year (a 6-3 win for Chelsea in the Carabao Cup). We will play twice more (in the league). We are ready for that. I like that. We will show that.'.

Calvert-Lewin shares similar attributes to Brobbey in that he is a traditional centre forward who will challenge Chelsea's centre backs.

Sources indicate that 'It¿s quite common in the Premier League that they have a good No 9,' Alonso said. 'Calvert-Lewin is doing well. He played with England. But it is up to us, how we defend, how we compete in those situations, how we attack the last line, how we attack their defenders. The preparation has, as always, we think been good. We are ready.'.

According to recent reports, asked if defenders have forgotten how to face such strikers, Alonso added: 'Forgotten? No, no, no, I don't think forgotten. But it's demanding to play against No 9s. They have good movement in the box, out the box. This is the demand. You can ask the full-backs, they have to play against great wingers in one v one situations. But I don't think it's been forgotten. But it's good they are back, these type of players.'.

Only Tottenham have made more changes to their line-up than Chelsea this season, adding to the suggestion that Alonso is still searching for his preferred style of play. Some have been forced on the Spaniard because of their habit for picking up injuries despite playing only once a week.

'Once you have the whole menu, you can select what you like and I know what I like from the menu,' Alonso mentioned. 'I would like to have more options with the whole squad available but that's something that's difficult to have during the season. I am sure we will get close to that.

'It (the injuries) is a concern. Sometimes you can analyse them and find a reason but sometimes it is difficult to find a reason.'.

According to recent reports, ‘Such behaviour only serves to cause hurt to others and does not represent the values we hold as a club. We want to create a safe and inclusive environment for all, and we have a shared responsibility in delivering this.’.

They added: ‘We understand that further incidents risk additional sanctions against the club and are doing everything we can to inform and educate supporters, as well as develop our existing initiatives to prevent, detect and respond to discrimination in future. We know Chelsea fans do not want to see any form of discrimination in our game, and we ask for their support in fostering a welcoming environment at Chelsea matches going forward.’.

On the pitch, Chelsea will go into their Saturday clash against Leeds United without star striker Joao Pedro, who has yet to return to training.

Since the Brazilian was sidelined, Chelsea have won only one of their three Premier League games played, beating a beleaguered Manchester United under Michael Carrick. Otherwise, they have lost to Tottenham Hotspur and Sunderland without scoring.

Industry observers note that joao Pedro is still nursing a thigh problem, and has not yet made it outside with his team-mates as Leeds visit Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Chelsea will, however, have Moises Caicedo available after his injury scare during the international break with Ecuador.

Sources indicate that ‘He's not fit yet to train with the team, so we need to wait a bit longer,’ Alonso confirmed on Joao Pedro. He’s not going to be available for Leeds. We need to see game by game how he's feeling. So far we have tried different options and we need to keep trying.’.

According to recent reports, chelsea will have Emiliano Martinez available after recovering from his broken jaw suffered at Everton on October 17. The goalkeeper required surgery following his collision with Jarrad Branthwaite. Alonso confirmed he no longer needs to wear a mask, having been training without it, and the 34-year-old Argentinian could be in line for his first club appearance since his injury.

Liverpool ‘showing concrete interest’ in Bundesliga wonderkid Jurgen Klopp likes

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (611 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Empireofthekop

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.
  • The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.
  • The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool are reportedly showing ‘concrete interest’ in highly-rated Gladbach talent Wael Mohya.

The Bundesliga teenager is high up on the list at German giants Bayern Munich, with the Bavarians expected to face competition from Bayer Leverkusen for his signature.

The attacking midfielder has registered four goal contributions in 11 games (across all competitions) this season.

According to recent reports, christian Falk told CF Bayern Insider: “However, Bayern Munich definitely have him on the list. And we should note that both Liverpool and Brighton in the Premier League are showing concrete interest in the 17-year-old attacking talent.

“This is why Gladbach would be well-advised to try and offer him a upcoming contract; that way, they can have some influence over how long the player stays at the club, or, at the very least, ensure that they get a sizeable sum from a permanent transfer.

Sources indicate that “I heard that there has already been contact with Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and they talked about a move to Leverkusen. The next step is to talk to the player, his family and then the club. He doesn’t have a long-term contract at Gladbach, so there is a chance to make this deal happen.”.

With a contract right now set to expire in the summer of 2028, Mohya represents a genuine market opportunity for clubs looking to invest in a high-potential option.

On that note, Brighton makes a great deal of sense as the next stop in the 17-year-old’s career (if not his final destination), similarly to Leverkusen in the German top-flight.

Liverpool, it has to be mentioned, would benefit greatly from a player with the Gladbach star’s profile, given they lack a viable backup option to Florian Wirtz in the ten position. Not to mention the fact that the footballer would provide further reassurance on the flanks.

Falk went on to add: “The 17-year-old was invited to the national team by Klopp during the international break. He wasn’t officially part of the squad; it was more just to give the player a taste of what international football looks like. He’s not totally clear yet about where he wants to commit, but Germany is putting up a strong fight to ensure that he pledges his international future to Die Nationalelf.”.

The big issue facing Mohya in the coming weeks and months, of course, is whether a move to the likes of FC Bayern and Liverpool are actually in his best interest at this stage in his career.

Bayern Munich have Ismael Saibari and Jamal Musiala behind Harry Kane, albeit there are question marks over the latter’s long-term future in Munich in light of ongoing concerns over his health.

Sources indicate that the Reds, of course, have Wirtz, in whom they invested a British transfer record fee (the total package being worth £116.5m). He’s played a significant percentage of the total minutes on offer in 2026/27 under fresh boss Andoni Iraola, and at 23 years of age, he’s hardly at any risk of sinking past his peak in the near future.

We’ve no doubt Liverpool would welcome having a rotational option of Mohya’s quality, whom they could develop on their own time, and they can supply evidence of how well they’re managing Rio Ngumoha’s development despite the presence of more senior figures in Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo.

But if Wael Mohya’s looking for an absolute guarantee of regular minutes, you could forgive him for either staying put in Germany or joining the talent factory line in Brighton.

Industry observers note that swansea City and Burnley are in contrasting positions in the Championship table, with the Swans still inside the play-offs and the Clarets stuck in the relegation zone. While both look to rediscover form on the pitch though, work is going on to identify potential targets for the January transfer window.

It has been revealed that now, a report from Football League World has claimed that the Championship pair are both interested in Huddersfield Town hotshot Joe Taylor. It is said that they are ‘weighing up’ moves for the 24-year-old striker as the next window approaches.

Recent findings suggest that taylor has been in excellent form this season with 12 goals and three assists in 18 games across all competitions. He is right now under contract until the summer of 2029; that and his form means it will take a handsome fee to prise him away from the Terriers this winter.

Despite his age and the fact he has moved around clubs a fair amount, Taylor is an established name in the EFL with 143 appearances to his bame across the Championship, League One and League Two.

Peterborough United signed him from non-league side Kings Lynn Town, and Luton Town bought him from there. Taylor impressed in loans with Colchester United (27 games, 12 goals, two assists) and Lincoln City (19 games, 10 goals, three assists) but failed to score in 19 outings for the Hatters.

Strong loan form prompted Huddersfield Town to snap him up, and Taylor’s Terriers career has come to life after another successful temporary move, this time to Wigan Athletic (22 games, 11 goals). The Welshman has proven to be a prolific scorer in League One and he is starring at the level once again, scoring for fun in Martin Drury’s attack alongside fellow star Derensili Sanches Fernandes.

Given his success in League One, it feels inevitable that Taylor gets another shot in the Championship. Swansea City and Burnley could offer him such a chance, but they will have to pay a good fee for his services.

Industry observers note that of the two interested clubs, Swansea City are no doubt the more attractive option at the moment. Despite the fact they are presently managerless, the Swans are in the hunt for a Championship play-off finish, and with the help of Jamestown Analytics, they are capable of making some long-awaited strides forward.

Recent findings suggest that but, for Taylor, a move to Burnley may be better. Swansea have all of Zan Vipotnik, Adam Idah and Ross Stewart on the books for their one-striker system, so they do not need another.

Recent findings suggest that as for the Clarets, they have plenty of strikers, but none are impressing. He would quickly jump up the pecking order and into contention for a starting spot against Jamie Vardy, Andreas Hountondji and Zeki Amdouni, and on current form, he’d be backed to beat them.

Alternatively though, a stay at Huddersfield Town could be best. The Terriers will have little interest in selling someone key to their promotion push, and he could end up in the Championship in their colours sooner rather than later.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under substantial pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6185 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, this was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

But then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

United were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent massive players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

According to recent reports, they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

The question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Recent findings suggest that afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical plan to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

Sources indicate that it was telling that so little did City’s latest head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their fresh head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

Maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a significant team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

In a recent development, the former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

Recent findings suggest that there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

Sources indicate that and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the problem then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

In a recent development, united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Sources indicate that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

Industry observers note that the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but massive moments in games like that have a big impact.

Industry observers note that we did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

In a recent development, we could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

[On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

It has been revealed that changed the initiative for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

Sources indicate that we always knew it was going to be a tough game. What happened with Phil at the start wasn’t good for us, but we said at half-time it would make us feel better if we win and we’ve taken three points.

In a recent development, it just gives you more motivation to go on and get the points. It was really tough for us. We had to run more and fight more. We all shone, to a man, and we were brilliant.

He was offside and what I can’t understand is it’s the rules... I went there because he was in front of him because that’s why Haaland was free at the back.

According to recent reports, every season they come to our club and spend an hour and a half explaining the rules, and they seem so confident with that, and then you have five or six people making this mistake. It’s unacceptable.

We have to go home with this injustice.

Recent findings suggest that haaland speaking on Sky: “We had to go low which is not ideal, we like to keep the ball, to try to score goals but in these times you have to go a bit low and take your chances when possible. We managed to do that well and that shows personality and character, to keep the ball away at Old Trafford with 10 men.”.

It has been revealed that “We had to change the plan a bit, but Enzo gave us a plan where we could play to our different strengths and counter-attack a bit more. For me personally, I just had to be there, to try to wait for a chance, and if there’s a chance, I had to be ready to execute. We also needed fighters in the team, which we have plenty of. Look at our midfield - it’s something they like to do! I’m so, so proud of everyone.”.

And on Donnarumma’s late save: “This wolf in goal giving you so much confidence, he looks a bit like a wolf. He is a mad man but he is a match-winner as well.”.

City win the Old Trafford derby with 10 men and Enzo Maresca runs down the touchline to celebrate in front of the travelling fans while their players embrace Donnarumma after his late save.

There will be so much analysis of Foden’s red card, but more so how Haaland’s winner stood given the final result. Should Enzo Fernandez have been considered offside?

In a recent development, but if you are judging performances, City are worthy winners. They defended stoutly, carried a threat and kept the ball well for periods even though they were a man light. United were aimless and froze.

A mammoth victory, and one which perhaps puts the breaks on talk of an Arsenal procession.

What a chance for Mbeumo to equalise! Superb save by Donnarumma, after the United forward was found by a Bruno Fernandes disguised pass into the box. Mbeumo took the ball under his spell and shot with power, but the substantial goalkeeper pushed the shot over the bar.

United have a corner, but Michael Oliver blows for a foul, and that is surely that.

In a recent development, martinez tries a straight ball towards Sesko, which is too high for the striker. United have perhaps just one more attack in them if they are too salvage a point.

Dalot with another poor cross that flies over everyone in the penalty area. Then Mainoo’s pass in midfield is intercepted by Anderson, and Ndiaye can bring the ball forward for City until he his tackled buy Martinez.

Fernandes drifts a cross behind for a City goal kick, between Sesko and Zirkzee and it looks like United are running out of time and ideas.

Recent findings suggest that dorgu with another foul on Ndiaye, yet another break in play for City. And there are going to just FIVE minutes of added time, much to Old Trafford’s frustration.

Haaland does well to bring City forward after another United attack breaks down, and Dorgu is penalised for a foul on Ndiaye. Another stoppage follows because the ball hits Michael Oliver. City can see the finish line so, and they would deserve their three points.

In a recent development, united have a corner after Guehi stands firm to block Cunha’s strike from distance. Maguire rises highest in the middle, but no United player gambled on the knockdown and his header drifts wide of the post.

Good work from Anderson against Mainoo in midfield, he receives a big cheer from the City fans. Carrick has thrown attackers on, but United have lost some structure and are not sustaining pressure.

Nico O’Reilly is now on for the closing stages, in place of Fernandez and Carrick has thrown on Zirkzee in place of Marcus Rashford. A United goal now would feel like a goal out of nowhere. City are playing the better football now and they have a corner.

United have lost all sense of momentum, City are keeping the ball for spells and then are happy for the game to be broken up stoppages.

Fernandez goes down looking for a penalty rather hopefully, and Maguire has been booked for his reaction as well as Fernandez for his role in the fracas. More and more time ticks away.

City are showing real resolve as well as quality here, Enzo Fernandez has just won a free-kick in the United half after a foul by Mainoo. The closest United have come in recent minutes was a glancing header wide from Mbeumo.

From that free-kick, Fernandez’s low delivery is close to being converted by Haaland or Guehi.

It’s a big final 16 minutes here plus injuries for United. You’re at home to your derby rivals who have been down to 10 men since the 23rd minute and you’ve had just two players show up for the mostpart so far - Mainoo and Rashford. The rest are really going to have to lift it.

Fernandes stings the palms of Donnarumma with a strike from outside the box.

Recent findings suggest that we have now had an explanation and evidence of why the goal stood. The VAR check for offside on Haaland found that he was in fact onside by fine margins, and that Fernandez (who was offside) did not affect Lisandro Martinez as he threw himself at a diving header (and missed). The Fernandez element feels the more debatable.

Recent findings suggest that city with a better sequence of passing but it does Ndiaye cannot get a shot away and then Fernandez commits another foul in midfield. Cunha with a poor cross behind for a City goal kick.

In a recent development, bryan Mbeumo with a wild shot over the bar after cutting inside from the right, Mainoo was involved in propelling United forward once again. Then Cunha shoots over from a tight angle, but United are knocking on the door now.

In a recent development, much better from United in the last few minutes, the crowd are engaged again and possibly for the first time in the game it feels like a goal might be coming. Nice idea from Rashford to let the ball run to Dorgu but the left-back is offside.

Sources indicate that kobbie Mainoo hits the post! Lovely strike from 25 yards after a Dalot pull-back is flicked into his path by Fernandes. Then United are back at the heart of the City defence, but Rashford’s shot deflects behind for a corner, from which the City goalkeeper is fouled.

Industry observers note that he’s been United’s best player by a distance so far this season and Kobbie Mainoo goes very close there to giving United the lead with a fine strike that hits the post. Next passage of play and he releases Rashford in on the left whose shot is pushed out for a corner.
