📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Southampton are propelling themselves back up the Championship table and Tonda Eckert, who had doubts over his future for off-field reasons, is now set to stay for the long-term at St Mary’s – but that could affect three Saints players.

Having been kicked out of the Championship play-offs ahead of the final last season due to ‘spygate’, Saints began this season with a four-point deduction in the second-tier and the prospect of a substantial ban coming for manager Eckert.

However, Eckert managed to escape with just a suspended six-match ban and so the club have now been able to tie him down to a newly introduced contract, too, ensuring the German is contracted to the south coast outfit until the summer of 2029.

Southampton eased past Derby County by two goals to nil at the weekend to leave them sixth in the table and just five points behind Middlesbrough, even with those four points taking off them at the start of the campaign.

Eckert is proving himself to be an excellent coach and having committed his future to the club, three players will now be looking for a permanent route out soon.

Having signed from Aston Villa in the summer of 2024 after previously impressing on loan at Preston North End and Middlesbrough in the Championship as well as an underwhelming stint in the Premier League with Sheffield United, Archer again struggled in the top-flight when with Southampton.

Having scored just two goals in 35 top-flight appearances for Saints as they succumbed to a humiliating relegation in which they collected just 12 points, Archer only notched four times in 30 Championship games last season – albeit with a slight improvement in his overall performance level before the end of the campaign before being an unused substitute in both legs of their play-off semi-final against ‘Boro.

Over the summer, he reunited with Will Still at Auxerre and has shone in Ligue 1 with six goals in nine appearances and, with no long-term future at Southampton, especially under Eckert, a permanent move in January or next summer feels inevitable.

Another loanee now destined to leave St Mary’s on a permanent basis is versatile Japan international full-back Yukinari Sugawara, who is at the moment out at Cagliari in Serie A.

Sugawara has been largely on the periphery of things in terms of the first-team picture in Sardinia, where he now a teammate of former Leicester City midfielder Harry Winks, and that is where he ended up at Southampton, too.

Having spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen in the Bundesliga, Sugawara’s permanent exit from Southampton has been expected for a while but, after a summer in which Eckert again sanctioned his departure, that is now inevitable. He is contracted to the club until the summer of 2028.

Upon their return to the Championship last summer, Southampton shelled out around £7 million on American forward Damion Downs but, from the off, he appeared to be surplus to requirements.

Injuries and generally average form eventually led to Downs being loaned out to Hamburg in the Bundesliga for the second half of last season, despite coming off the bench in Eckert’s first four matches in charge of Saints last November before his injury.

An indifferent time of it at the Volksparkstadion was then followed by the 22-year-old being shipped out to St Louis City on loan this summer, where he has failed to score in ten MLS appearances as the expansion franchise finished third in the Western Conference and now head into the play-offs.

Downs is contracted until the summer of 2029 but a permanent move away in the winter after the close of the 2026 MLS campaign feels inevitable, even if he hasn’t done enough for St Louis to take the plunge on him just yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A statistic has been doing the rounds regarding Ruben Amorim’s league record with AC Milan, which is gathering some attention.

His style of play is open to criticism, his selections are controversial, his words are regularly quite strong and he’s often called into question at the first sign of failure. For Amorim, his first months with the Rossoneri have been a rollercoaster ride.

It has been revealed that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

There have been ups and downs: things have been better domestically, culminating in a derby victory over Inter, but in the Europa League the one win from four games means the Rossoneri currently sit outside the playoff zone.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write, there is a key bit of data to contextualise things. With 24 points in his first 11 Serie A matches, Amorim is averaging 2.18 points per game, the result of seven wins, three draws, and one defeat.

Sources indicate that it is the highest ever for a Milan coach in the three-point era, ahead of Stefano Pioli, Carlo Ancelotti and Massimiliano Allegri. Looking at coaches with at least five stints in the Italian top flight, only Antonio Conte boasts a better figure than the Portuguese coach, with 2.21 points per game.

This is obviously an unfair comparison, given that the former Napoli coach’s points average takes into account all 279 of his Serie A games – with spells at Atalanta, Juventus, Inter and Napoli – compared to just 11 for the former United manager.

It has been revealed that however, it is a testament to the excellent work done thus far by Amorim and his staff. Even more so in a season in which the decision was made to undertake a revolution in several respects, to relaunch a team and a fan base that had been burned by the collapse of last season.

According to recent reports, gerry Cardinale and the ownership made significant investments during the last transfer window, spending €70m on Goncalo Ramos and €50m on Diego Moreira, plus €25m on Mario Gila. This is also why Milan fans have high expectations for Amorim’s era.

In a recent development, to date, the average from these first 11 games project the Rossoneri to land around 83 points by the end of the season. Last year, Inter won the Scudetto with 87 points, and 71 were needed to finish fourth, the minimum target set by the owners.

Allegri’s Milan stopped at 70 points, despite a strong start to the season that even fuelled a few Scudetto dreams for a few months. That start, however, was inferior to this season: a year ago, after 11 matchdays, AC Milan had 22 points, two fewer than under Amorim.

It is an encouraging beginning to the newly introduced era that fans hope will translate into concrete results, perhaps even the Scudetto, a target confirmed by owner Cardinale as a real aim, as unrealistic as it may have seemed before a ball was kicked.

Amorim is trying to convey his vision of football and instil a more European mentality in his team, and the numbers so far – at least in the league – seem to prove him right. To find a better start to a season one must rewind to 2022-23, when Milan had 26 points from 11 games under Pioli.

Ruben Amorim has the highest points-per-game average of any #ACMilan coach in Serie A in the three-points-per-win era: 2.18 over 11 matches.

Among all coaches with 5+ stints in the league during that period, only Antonio Conte (2.21) has a higher average.

[via @OptaPaolo] pic.twitter.com/jwPLgVw0z7.

— MilanData📊 (@acmilandata) November 19, 2026.

Speaking of Pioli, in the specific ranking of Milan coaches with the highest points average – led by Amorim, as mentioned – the coach who led the Rossoneri to their 19th Scudetto (2021-22) occupies second place at 2.02 points per game in 183 Serie A matches.

Pioli also achieved the best start in Milan’s history: in the Scudetto year, he earned 31 points from the opening 11 games, the result of 10 wins and 1 draw, with a record average of 2.82 points per game.

In third place among Milan coaches with the highest points average is Ancelotti, with 1.95 points in 283 Serie A games as Milan coach. Allegri is just off the podium, with 1.91 points in 172 games across his two spells at the club.

To compare Amorim with two of his compatriots who recently worked at Milanello, Paulo Fonseca averaged just 1.59 points per game from 17 games, while Sergio Conceicao fared slightly better with 1.71 points in 21 games.

Recent findings suggest that in short, Amorim’s performance is encouraging, but still relative given the very limited sample size. A crucial month is now beginning for Milan: a seven-game tour de force before Christmas that will reveal a lot about the true ambitions of the coach and his team, with form in Europe to fix.

Spurs finally score... but still lose

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.
  • It could have been something different.
  • According to recent reports, “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

They scored. Would you believe it? Tottenham Hotspur, the team with more zeroes than an England Ashes batting collapse, found the back of the net but still frustration persists for Roberto De Zerbi.

It could have been something different. The sight of the Italian dashing down the touchline in hailstones, grabbing his head in disbelief in the final seconds, showed this was not a straightforward tale of misery but, ultimately, the misery endures.

According to recent reports, “I think this is five or six games we have been for sure not lucky,” De Zerbi lamented, but sympathy did not extend too far. Liverpool deservedly moved into the next round of the Carabao Cup, the gloss on Andoni Iraola’s most enjoyable night provided by Dominik Szoboszlai’s goal-of-the-season contender.

THAT'S MAGNIFICENT! 💥🔴Outrageous strike from Dominik Szoboszlai 👏👏👏 pic.twitter.com/meQ7nilsz6.

Liverpool were abject against Fulham on Saturday but with 10 changes to the starting line-up, infused with the exuberance of novices Rio Ngumoha and the terrific Lewis Koumas, Iraola’s team were invigorated and only a lapse of concentration enabled Tottenham to make a fist of it.

Yes, they went down swinging, as their noisy fans demanded. But carelessness cannot be excused and while De Zerbi complained about bad luck, a bad miss from Lucas Bergvall in the 10th minute was the fork in the road for the tie. Tottenham stalled and Liverpool never looked back.

Industry observers note that “We have to shoot more times and we have to shoot better,” De Zerbi harrumphed. “We have to finish better the clear situations. We are sorry for the result, disappointed and frustrated. I think it was unfair but we have to be stronger in these unlucky moments.”.

According to recent reports, rather than fizzing his drive into the net, Bergvall succeeded only in firing straight at Giorgi Mamardashvili, when he had the whole target in front of him. It was, in all fairness, a brilliant save but he should never have been allowed to make it.

According to recent reports, major save from Giorgi Mamardashvili! 💪Lucas Bergvall is denied by the Liverpool goalkeeper. pic.twitter.com/fKUbfGLMku.

Industry observers note that the miss changed the atmosphere, as suddenly Liverpool grasped the need to be competitive. At the heart of it all were Ngumoha, James McConnell, Trey Nyoni and Koumas, the last-named a nuisance to Tottenham’s defenders in the way a wasp is to picnickers on a summer’s afternoon.

According to recent reports, for all the money that has been lavished by this club over the past 14 months, the one thing that the locals buy into more than anything is the basics done properly: hard work, tackling, a refusal to take second best. Iraola did not want Koumas to go anywhere this summer and it was obvious why.

In a recent development, “I see him training every day,” Iraola said. “He knows very clearly what he needs to do, what the team needs. And also the energy he highlights is contagious for the rest. When you see the runs up front, giving everything, you are kind of forced to go behind and use the same intensity levels.”.

Simple tenacity enabled Liverpool to get back on an even keel and laid the foundation for them to take the lead. It was a terrific goal, started with a raking pass from Joe Gomez that Cody Gakpo controlled instantly on his chest before scuttling inside and inviting Ngumoha to charge forward.

Whether it was the winger or Destiny Udogie, who was sliding to make a challenge, that ended up playing the ball to Alexis Mac Allister is immaterial, all that mattered is that the Argentine effortlessly placed his shot into the top corner, leaving Martin Dubravka planted and helpless.

According to recent reports, pick that out!! 🇦🇷Alexis Mac Allister hits a beauty into the roof of the net 🔴 pic.twitter.com/G7OT27CA8P.

It has been revealed that is Mac Allister playing with a point to prove? Possibly, given his comments about not being offered a new contract last week. Will Iraola be bothered? Not in the slightest. All he wants is top players at the top of their game and Mac Allister is climbing towards the levels he highlighted two years ago.

What De Zerbi would do to have a player in such form, but Tottenham are a skittish bunch, not the type of team who respond well in the face of adversity and their head coach, dressed in black with his oversized white trainers, regularly shook his head in exasperation.

Industry observers note that his mood was not helped just before the interval, when Mohammed Kudus blasted over from eight yards following a zipped-in cross from Udogie, but he would not have called it truthfully if he had suggested Tottenham deserved parity at that stage. Soon Liverpool’s advantage would be doubled.

The buffer they sought arrived in the 54th minute and, again, it was another genuinely attractive goal, with possession being kept until it sped up when Ngumoha scurried forward, found Milos Kerkez, who played it to Mac Allister, who in turn gave Gakpo the opening he craved.

Sources indicate that his touch was excellent, his finish was even better and away in the distance Iraola rattled his fists in delight. That is two goals and four assists to start the campaign for the Dutchman and yet Liverpool were ready to sell him to Manchester City two weeks ago. What on earth were they thinking?

Industry observers note that ruthless!! 🔥Cody Gakpo doubles Liverpool's lead against Spurs 🔴 pic.twitter.com/qlaaynMuwM.

Sources indicate that from that point, it seemed inconceivable that Liverpool would finish living on their nerves, but De Zerbi’s decision to introduce Andy Robertson – given a hero’s reception on his first return to Anfield – and Mateus Fernandes wrestled back some impetus. There was also a significant helping hand.

Unsurprisingly, Andy Robertson gets a great reception from the Liverpool fans on his return to Anfield 👏 pic.twitter.com/uNM6A00k5F.

Mamardashvili had made some important saves, including one from Kudus that he celebrated on his own, but he is vulnerable at set-pieces and Fernandes’s looping corner gave Conor Gallagher the easiest headed opportunity in three years to change the dynamic.

According to recent reports, spurs have scored! ⚪️Conor Gallagher brings Roberto De Zerbi's side back into the game! pic.twitter.com/52zSCqClw4.

“We were under pressure at the end, but I don’t think we were nervous,” Gakpo remarked.

He was right. Try as they might, Spurs could not quite get the opening they needed and as they chased in vain, Szoboszlai administered the final blow in mesmerising fashion, thrashing a bouncing ball into the Kop net from 30 yards. And as De Zerbi realised in the sodden conditions, with Tottenham it never rains. It only pours.

Tottenham Hotspur did not pay Roberto De Zerbi, their head coach, a survival bonus for keeping the club in the Premier League and now Spurs are saving a fortune on goal bonuses.

De Zerbi’s team are yet to score against Premier League opposition this season and face Liverpool in the third round of the Carabao Cup at Anfield on Tuesday night.

A place in the League Cup fourth round is at stake at Anfield as Liverpool host Tottenham in an all-Premier League tie.

Liverpool were frustrated on the weekend, being held to a 0-0 draw at home against Fulham, meaning they have one win and three draws from their opening four league games.

According to recent reports, “I am very happy with the squad,” Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola stated. “I value a lot my players, if we win games, the squad will look amazing and fantastic, if we do not there is going to be a problem with the depth. I think we will see also tomorrow [tonight] players we have not seen still and I am really looking forward to seeing. I feel they are going to play well and help us and they still have not had their chance. You can decide and put the same players in every game. The problem is there will be a moment when they are really tired. And there is more risk of injury.

It has been revealed that “But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no challenges. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is newly introduced, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”.

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi remarked. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have major confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”.

Tottenham’s League Cup journey last season came to an end in the fourth round last season, losing 2-0 at Newcastle. Sandro Tonali and Pedro Porro will not be involved tonight for the visitors and neither will Richarlison, who has been left out. Andrew Robertson returns to Anfield for the first time after leaving Liverpool in the summer following nine years on Merseyside.

Team news from Anfield to follow shortly.

Yunus Musah has insisted that AC Milan must believe in the Scudetto, while also assessing his start to the campaign under Ruben Amorim.

Going into the summer, an uncertain fate awaited Musah. Massimiliano Allegri did not see him as a part of the plans for 2025-26 and so he was loaned to Atalanta, where he had a mixed year and ultimately returned as they did not use their option to buy him.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Many sources presumed that it would be a return in passing and that a upcoming destination would be found, but Amorim had other plans. The new coach clearly saw something in the USA international, and he has become a regular starter regardless of the system used.

Such is his importance, there is even talk of a renewal being discussed. Musah was interviewed by SportMediaset and it was published two days before the Serie A campaign resumes with a home game against Frosinone. His comments were transcribed by MilanNews.

Do you feel like a ‘wild card’ for Milan?

Recent findings suggest that “A little less so this year because I haven’t changed positions as much, even though I can do that. I’ve been able to play in midfield and improve in that area.”.

It has been revealed that “I think he watched my old games, because he already knew what he expected from me and what he could ask of me. He did his homework, he watched everything, and he already knew what and how he could use me.”.

We’ve never seen you play left-back at Milan like you did in Genoa: how did this idea come about?

It has been revealed that “I don’t know (laughs). This question is for the coach. Bartesaghi and Estupinan are very good, but that day he wanted a right-footed player on the left.”.

If it were up to you, where do you want to play most?

In a recent development, “I think playing in midfield. Not fixed, though, being able to go anywhere so I can get the ball, get deep, without being fixed.”.

Do you think Milan is improving? Is the Scudetto possible?

“It’s possible. We train every day for it. We all have the dream and ambition of winning it, and we’ll do everything we can to get there.”.

Can you tell us what you remember about your time in the States?

What do you remember about America?

“Playing for the United States helped me gain this sense of belonging. Until I was 17, I only had a passport, but now I feel part of the culture.”.

“I can go there. I know the restaurants, the chains, the people from different states, the geography. I understand American people so much now.

“I have many passports, I lived and grew up in many countries, like here in Italy, in England, so I feel a bit of everything.”.

Have you ever returned to see your childhood homes?

“Yes, in 2021 I returned to New York. I saw the house where I lived that year. The Bronx. It was beautiful to see it. There was a piece missing from my memory, and it was nice to be able to connect it.”.

Is it true you have a cat named Bronx?

“Yes. I left him with the neighbours in Valencia because I couldn’t take him to Milan.”.

Your family moved from America to Italy….

“My family was already in Italy, and my mother had to go back and forth to America.”.

What was your childhood like in Castelfranco Veneto?

In a recent development, “Beautiful. It’s a place where my parents weren’t afraid to let me play all day outside in the parking lot near the apartment building.”.

Is it true that your parents’ years of financial sacrifice were years of financial hardship?

“Of course. Obviously, when I grew up, we weren’t rich, we didn’t have much money, but from the time I left home, even when I was little, my parents never let me go without anything. I hope I’m their pride, because they are mine.”.

According to recent reports, you have also played for Arsenal and Valencia. What were the transitions like?

“Playing for Arsenal was a great privilege, because I arrived from Italy at 9 years old, played with a small team, and immediately joined Arsenal.

It has been revealed that “I was ready to move to the first team when I was 16, and Valencia had a plan for me. I spent four wonderful years in Spain; it’s a city that will always remain in my heart.”.

What’s the atmosphere like in the dressing room?

“Last year I watched them a lot; they were a very solid team and difficult to beat. Amorim brought a very positive vibe, we understand each other. He understands the player very well and vice versa.

“It helps when he understands what the players need; he’s good at that, and the players in the team are pretty calm.”.

Is he someone who gets angry when necessary?

Recent findings suggest that “Yes. After Ferencvaros he was very angry, like everyone else.”.

What ties do you have to Africa?

Recent findings suggest that “My wife is from Zanzibar, my family is Ghanaian. So it’s nice to travel to our home countries in the summer.”.

Industry observers note that “Heaven, I’d loan him out, get some experience in the Championship. He’s nowhere near it, it’s unfair to put him in the situation he’s in,” Neville said on Stick to Football.

Recent findings suggest that in midfield, Neville wants Pochettino to build around Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans. He also believes Andrey Santos could have a future at the club because of his age, mobility and aggression.

Mason Mount, however, is not part of his aims. Neville noted: “Mount would have to go” and identified him as the player to leave from that midfield group.

Sources indicate that neville also has his doubts on the forward line, with much of the front line seeing a change. Gary Neville expects Joshua Zirkzee to leave and believes United cannot continue paying Marcus Rashford’s wages.

Recent findings suggest that “Zirkzee definitely to go. I think Marcus 100 per cent to go because he’s on massive money and that story has been well told. They can’t afford to pay him that money, you have to get rid of that wage at the earliest opportunity.”.

He expects Pochettino to work with Amad Diallo, Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha and Benjamin Sesko. Patrick Dorgu could also be useful in the short term, although Neville thinks he may leave within the next couple of years. Manuel Ugarte, meanwhile, was another player he was certain would go.

Talking about the exits, Gary Neville has singled out many United stars to be shown the door in the first wave of squad clearance by Mauricio Pochettino. Neville identified Lisandro Martínez, Matthijs de Ligt and Noussair Mazraoui as further candidates to leave in the first wave of departures, alongside Mount, Rashford and Zirkzee.

According to recent reports, neville believes another group of exits could follow a year later, with Shaw, Maguire, Diogo Dalot and Fernandes among the players whose futures may not be at the club in long term. Pochettino would also have to decide whether Santos and Carlos Baleba fit into his long-term looks.

Neville does not expect United to rebuild the squad in a single summer, even if Pochettino makes a positive start.

“But the earliest Mauricio Pochettino can unravel this squad is two seasons if he does well. It could take three to get this squad unravelled.”.

Pochettino’s first game comes against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday. His immediate priority will be to get some results for Manchester United but beyond the immediate games and results, Manchester United are expected to make multiple exits from the club as Pochettino settles into the job.

Wolverhampton Wanderers could go top of the Championship on Tuesday night when they host Derby County at Molineux, whilst the Rams aim to get a much-needed three points on the road amid a scrap towards the foot of the table.

Wolves have leapfrogged Birmingham City in the Championship to go 3rd, just one point behind Middlesbrough and Stoke City ahead of them, as depending on how Boro get on at home to Swansea City, the Old Gold could go top for the evening.

Cesar Peixoto's side are undefeated in their last seven league games, with their most recent defeat coming at home to Bolton Wanderers, as Derby will hope to follow in the footsteps of the Trotters on Tuesday.

Pressure on John Eustace is increasing, with just two wins in 16 games this season, and with only Preston North End beneath them in the table, a win would be huge for the Rams.

Wolves certainly come into this clash the favourites, but Eustace will do everything in his power to give his Derby side the best possible chance of a result, as Football League World takes a closer look at the absentees of this fixture.

Mexican striker Raul Jimenez is set to miss the rest of the calendar year after going in for knee surgery in mid-October, in a huge blow for Wolves, having re-signed the 35-year-old on a free transfer over the summer.

With three goals and one assist in six Championship games this season, Jimenez has displayed he is still a capable goalscorer despite his age, as Wolves head coach Cesar Peixoto will be eager to see him return to action in the new year, with Adam Armstrong, Sean Neave, and Tawanda Chirewa each vying for a place up top as things stand.

Following Peixoto to Wolves this summer was Ivorian left-back Ghislain Konan, with the 30-year-old adding another option in that area of the pitch following his release from Gil Vicente.

However, after just three appearances in all competitions, the defender has been sidelined until late December after picking up an MCL injury, and will certainly play no role in this clash.

A substantial blow for Derby, as star attacking midfielder Sammie Szmodics remains on the sidelines until near the end of the year after suffering a knee injury in the Rams' 4-0 home defeat to Norwich City.

Signing a permanent deal at Pride Park in the summer from Ipswich Town after a successful loan spell, Eustace will have to make do without the 31-year-old, with his attacking output a crucial miss for his side.

Danish striker Henrik Meister joined Derby on loan from Italian side Pisa late into the summer window to provide another option up top alongside Carlton Morris and Lars-Jorgen Salvesen.

The 23-year-old, who has yet to really show what he is capable of since arriving at Pride Park, replaced Mohammed Fuseini just on the hour mark in the Rams' 2-0 defeat away to Southampton, but had to be taken off 20 minutes later after injuring his shoulder.

The extent of the injury, at this stage, remains unclear, but he's not expected to feature in this one.

Veteran full-back Craig Forsyth has been out of action since the beginning of September, coming off in the latter stages of Derby's 2-0 away victory to Portsmouth, which remains their only three points on the road this season.

The 37-year-old was expected to be out for at least a couple of months, and now approaching three, it appears as though this setback has taken longer than hoped, as he is not expected to feature in this one.

Joining Derby from Dutch outfit Utrecht in January 2026, English full-back Derry Murkin has yet to make a single appearance this season after suffering an injury back in April.

Further damage to his hamstring during pre-season set him back for a further four months, and upon his return to action, he will be a welcome addition to the side.

Norwegian defender Sondre Langås compiled misery for Derby in their 4-1 away defeat to Queens Park Rangers back in mid-October, suffering a groin injury which keeps him out of action until the newly introduced year.

The 25-year-old was taken off just 12 minutes into the clash, and if Derby want to avoid a relegation battle this season, his return to fitness ASAP is of the utmost importance.

Who do you think will be the biggest miss from this clash, and what are your score predictions? Share your thoughts below!

English left-back Charlie Taylor has been out of action since mid-September after suffering an injury late in Derby's 1-1 draw away with Burnley.

The defender is still recovering from a hamstring problem and will be absent for the trip to Molineux.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea, according to ESPN.

Brady was in attendance at the MetLife Stadium in New Jersey when Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

NFL icon Tom Brady has purchased a small stake in Premier League giants Chelsea.

Brady watched Chelsea beat Paris Saint-Germain 3-0 in the 2025 Club World Cup final.

At Birmingham, Brady made headlines when he questioned Wayne Rooney’s work ethic during a documentary following his time at St Andrew’s.

Rooney, who went on to be sacked after just 15 games in charge, later described those comments as ‘very unfair’.

In a recent development, when Brady exited Birmingham, the club remarked in a statement: ‘Birmingham City Football Club expresses its sincere gratitude to Tom Brady for his involvement with and unwavering support for the club over the last three years. It was truly amazing to have someone with Tom’s experience and passion associated with the club, and the club looks forward to continuing to build on that foundation from the training ground to the Birmingham community.’.

Chelsea have invited minority shareholders with their women’s team.

NBA star Giannis Antetokounmpo previously purchased a stake in the side, partnering with Alexis Ohanian, the founder of social media platform Reddit who likewise invested in the team in 2025.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.
  • Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel.
  • The footage revealed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session was secretly filmed by a drone operator, who has since apologised and removed the footage from his YouTube channel after admitting his actions were unethical.

Around 12 minutes of footage from Carrington was recorded on Thursday and uploaded to a YouTube channel. The video offered supporters an early glimpse of Mauricio Pochettino working with his latest squad, but its release promptly raised concerns about the privacy of United’s training sessions.

The footage revealed players split into smaller groups carrying out different drills. On a separate full-size pitch, 11 players were positioned across the field alongside mannequins before gathering to receive instructions and feedback from upcoming head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Ten players were seen working with Pochettino in the video but only Harry Maguire, Kobbie Mainoo, Amad Diallo, Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbeumo are regular starters among those.

Another group involved in drills was that of Lisandro Martinez, Matthijs de Ligt, Youri Tielemans, Mason Mount, Leny Yoro, Noussair Mazraoui and Diogo Dalot.

After backlash from fans over the breach of privacy, the video was removed on Friday morning, with the operator issuing an apology for filming the session.

In his statement, the operator mentioned the flight itself was legal under drone regulations but accepted that recording the training session was wrong.

He explained that his intention was to give Manchester United supporters their first look at Pochettino wearing the club’s training kit.

He mentioned: “A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.”.

The operator apologized directly to the club, its fresh head coach and the players.

“I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.”.

He also rejected any suggestion that Liverpool or another football club had been involved in his decision to film at Carrington.

“The video has been removed from my channel,” he added.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jamie Carragher believes Mauricio Pochettino has as much to prove as Manchester United, suggesting the Argentine’s reputation is not fully backed up by his achievements.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing for his first match in charge of Manchester United against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, following his departure from the United States national team to replace Michael Carrick.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea manager has arrived at Old Trafford with plenty of experience, but Carragher believes his appointment represents an opportunity for both United and Pochettino to rebuild their reputations.

Writing in The Telegraph, the former Liverpool defender highlighted the irony of United turning to a manager whose own career needs a fresh start.

“It is ironic that in their latest attempt to rejuvenate and restore some of their old fire, Manchester United have turned to a manager whose career needs a similar reawakening,” Carragher wrote.

He suggested that Pochettino should be grateful that a club of United’s stature came calling at this stage of his career.

Recent findings suggest that “Manchester United need a savior to first ease them from the relegation zone and then revive their Premier League and Champions League credibility. Pochettino, meanwhile, needed a club like United to save him from a managerial career that promised more than it delivered.”.

Manchester United were fortunate to secure a manager with Pochettino’s experience after dismissing Michael Carrick so early in the season. However, he believes the Argentine has plenty to prove despite his strong reputation in the game.

“The South American returns to England with a big reputation, but not enough on his CV to back up glowing testimonials,” he continued.

Carrick believes one of the biggest concerns surrounding Pochettino is his record in key matches.

“A recurring concern with Pochettino, which continued with the US team, is an inability to get over the line in the most consequential, winnable matches, resulting in a lack of significant trophies.”.

Despite questioning his ability to bottle in major games, he praised his teams when everything comes in together.

“Ten years ago his best team were the embodiment of him, full of energy, style and ambition. Time will tell whether this version of Pochettino is the one turning up at Old Trafford.”.

According to recent reports, pochettino will have the chance to shut Carragher’s doubts on Sunday when Manchester United face Liverpool. His immediate priority will be to take United out of the relegation zone, but the expectations at Old Trafford will extend far beyond survival.

It has been revealed that the Liverpool fixture will be his first opportunity to make an impression. Carragher, however, believes the Argentine’s real challenge is to turn his reputation into success.

  • “Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino noted in his first Manchester United press conference.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has made it clear he wants to be involved in Manchester United’s major squad decisions, while also addressing questions surrounding captain Bruno Fernandes ahead of his first game against Liverpool.

The upcoming Manchester United head coach explained that he wants to have a voice in decisions that shape the squad.

“Sometimes maybe you are a coach and maybe you have more power in the decisions,” Pochettino noted in his first Manchester United press conference.

“It depends on the structure, it depends on the communication, the relationships, you know, with all the areas.”.

Mauricio Pochettino highlighted his responsibilities are clear about who he selects and plays in games.].

“I am the guy that is going to decide the squad for Sunday, and I’m going to pick the team, I’m going to make the changes, and of course in the future, I would like to be involved in all the main decisions that will happen on the squad.”.

Pochettino was also asked about Bruno Fernandes, whose critical comments about Michael Carrick’s tactics became a talking point during the former manager’s final weeks at Old Trafford.

The Argentine was really keen about the squad’s commitment, dodging the blame on Fernandes and describing Fernandes as a key figure in the dressing room.

“The commitment from all the players was amazing from day one,” he noted.

“Bruno is our captain and a very key player but all the players need to feel they are important from the bottom to the top.”.

Pochettino revealed that he had already spent time speaking with the players to understand their situation both on and off the pitch.

“Yesterday we spent three hours chatting to the players in my office and maybe I missed the injured players.”.

Pochettino admitted the first few days at United had been extremely busy as he tried to get up to speed before his first match.

He is excited by the opportunity but knows there is little time to prepare for Sunday’s trip to Anfield.

“It’s a happy time but at the same time, so busy,” he explained.

“It’s been about adapting in the last few days, and it’s a race to arrive in condition to be competitive against Liverpool, and now our focus is 100 per cent on Liverpool in the game on Sunday.”.

Sankhoun Diawara would thus take the left centre-back spot, with either Davide Bartesaghi or Pervis Estupinan covering the left flank. The defence will be completed by Koni De Winter and Mario Gila, with the Spaniard operating on the right again.

It has been revealed that in midfield, Yunus Musah, Luka Modric and Adrian Rabiot – who could play in a more advanced, attacking-midfield role – are expected to be the starting trio. In attack, Diego Moreira and Goncalo Ramos are guaranteed starters, with Christian Pulisic at the moment favoured over Alphadjo Cisse.

Predicted Milan XI (4-2-3-1): Maignan; Gila, De Winter, Diawara, Bartesaghi; Musah, Modric; Pulisic, Rabiot, Moreira; Ramos.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis, Schmid, Kvernadze; Birligea.

Industry observers note that for supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

In a recent development, the concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Then there is the defensive side.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring problem ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader matter was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

It has been revealed that caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.
  • United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.
  • The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have spent approximately £95m appointing and dismissing managers since Sir Alex Ferguson retired in 2013, according to BBC Sport, with the total expected to pass £100m following Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival.

United’s latest financial disclosures confirm a fee of £7.584m in connection with appointing Pochettino, who left his role as United States national team head coach earlier this month.

The figure takes the cumulative cost of managerial changes to around £95m, according to BBC Sport’s analysis. That total is expected to rise once the costs of Michael Carrick’s dismissal and appointing Pochettino’s coaching staff are included.

Pochettino signed a two-and-a-half-year contract on 13 November, replacing Carrick after a difficult start to the Premier League season. The club’s Stock Market filing states that the appointment fee will be recognised in its financial accounts for the current quarter. United also confirmed borrowing a further £10m on 16 November, taking the amount drawn on their revolving credit facility to £240m.

In a recent development, pochettino is United’s ninth full-time managerial appointment since Ferguson’s departure, including Ralf Rangnick’s interim spell. The club have also changed managers during each of the past three seasons.

It has been revealed that united’s financial disclosures show that their long-term debt stood at £577.4m on 30 September, while outstanding transfer-fee commitments totalled £417m. Those figures are separate from the cost of appointing and dismissing managers.

A Reuters analysis has put the wider cost of managerial and senior football staff changes above £100m, using a broader calculation. Pochettino now faces the task of improving United’s results, beginning with Sunday’s Premier League trip to Liverpool.

Liverpool v Manchester United: Five classic wins at Anfield

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (678 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Readmanutd

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.
  • With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.
  • United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

From Diego Forlan’s unforgettable double to Juan Mata’s spectacular volley, Manchester United have enjoyed some memorable victories at Anfield over the years.

With Mauricio Pochettino preparing for his first match in charge against Liverpool on Sunday, we look back at five occasions when United emerged victorious from one of English football’s fiercest fixtures.

United travelled to Anfield on 19 April 1997 knowing Liverpool could overtake them at the top of the Premier League with a victory. Instead, centre-back Gary Pallister scored twice with headers from David Beckham deliveries, either side of John Barnes’s equaliser.

Andy Cole added a third after the interval, heading home from Gary Neville’s cross following an error by Liverpool goalkeeper David James. The victory helped Sir Alex Ferguson’s side take a decisive step towards retaining the Premier League title, which they secured the following month.

Fresh from winning the Treble, United returned to Anfield for a remarkable match in September 1999. Jamie Carragher headed into his own net inside three minutes before Andy Cole doubled United’s advantage.

Recent findings suggest that sami Hyypia pulled a goal back for Liverpool, but Carragher’s second own goal restored the visitors’ two-goal lead. Patrik Berger reduced the deficit again, and United faced a difficult finish after Cole was sent off for a second bookable offence. Despite playing the closing stages with 10 men, Ferguson’s side held on for a 3-2 victory.

Diego Forlan had endured a frustrating start to his United career before producing a performance that supporters would remember for years. The Uruguayan opened the scoring after Liverpool goalkeeper Jerzy Dudek failed to gather the ball, allowing him to finish from close range.

Industry observers note that forlan added a second just minutes later, beating Dudek at his near post to put United in control. Sami Hyypia pulled one back for Liverpool, but Ferguson’s side held on for a victory that proved valuable in their successful pursuit of the 2002-03 Premier League title. Forlan’s double also inspired a terrace song that remains familiar to United supporters.

Few United victories at Anfield have been as dramatic as the one secured by John O’Shea in March 2007. Liverpool had enjoyed the better opportunities, and United’s task became harder when Paul Scholes was sent off late in the second half.

With a goalless draw appearing increasingly likely, Cristiano Ronaldo’s free-kick was parried by goalkeeper Pepe Reina. Substitute O’Shea reacted quickest, firing the rebound high into the net in stoppage time. The unexpected winner gave United three valuable points on their way to reclaiming the Premier League title.

Juan Mata produced one of the most memorable individual performances in this fixture during Louis van Gaal’s first season as United manager. The Spaniard opened the scoring after 14 minutes, finishing a move involving Ander Herrera, before doubling United’s lead with a spectacular scissor-kick volley after half-time.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool captain Steven Gerrard had been sent off just 38 seconds after coming on as a substitute at the interval. Daniel Sturridge reduced the deficit, while Wayne Rooney missed a late penalty, but United held on for a 2-1 victory. Mata’s second goal remains one of the outstanding moments of United’s Premier League visits to Anfield.

Those five victories underline the different ways United have succeeded at Anfield, from outstanding individual performances to late winners and determined defensive displays. Pochettino now has an opportunity to begin his managerial reign with a memorable result against United’s biggest rivals.

By WILL PICKWORTH, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 02:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 04:21 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cristiano Ronaldo may have finally departed the international stage, but he still remained a major part of Portugal's story over the past week.

That came after they suffered a humiliating 4-1 defeat by Denmark in the first game since his retirement, their heaviest home loss in competitive history.

In the aftermath of that match, Ronaldo's mother Dolores launched a furious and unprompted attack on the national team, claiming the defeat was just, and added she was happy to see the result.

Despite an emotional and historic tribute to Ronaldo pre-game, Dolores also expressed her unhappiness at what had unfolded, before she claimed the veteran's former international team-mates failed to show him the respect he deserved during his career.

Dolores has not always been an outspoken presence over the years, but has often stepped up to defend her son when she feels necessary.

So, in light of her outburst, Daily Mail Sport has taken a look at other examples of when the mums of footballers have got involved in their careers.

Cristiano Ronaldo's mum became embroiled in her son's row with Portugal's national team after saying she was happy to see them suffer a heavy defeat (Source: Instagram/doloresaveiroofficial).

Veronique Rabiot – Adrien Rabiot.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique has developed a reputation as an uncompromising and fiercely protective negotiator in her role as his agent.

This has seen the French midfielder face several flashpoints in his career, beginning  when Veronique pulled him out of Man City's academy after just six months in 2008 because she felt they were not looking after his interests like they should be.

During his time at PSG, where Rabiot ultimately broke through and spent seven seasons in the first team, Veronique then frequently clashed with the club's hierarchy.

Potential transfers to Roma and Man United during his career have also both collapsed late on, a factor some reports attach to Veronique's role in the deals.

There have been several notable flashpoints on the international stage too, not least when she backed her son's controversial decision to withdraw from France's standby list for the 2018 World Cup.

But that was nothing compared to the aftermath of France's shock exit from Euro 2020 at the last-16 stage.

Veronique made headlines at the time for engaging in a heated confrontation with the parents of Kylian Mbappe and the entourage of Paul Pogba in the stands over on-pitch errors and perceived arrogance during Les Bleus' campaign.

Adrien Rabiot's mother Veronique (centre) has developed a reputation as a formidable force.

As the mother of one of the best footballers on the planet, Fayza Lamari was always likely to be a major powerbroker, and she has played a key role in Kylian Mbappe's career, acting as his chief negotiator and business manager.

This has seen Fayza oversee Mbappe's commercial obligations and image rights, while she played a central role in his dramatic contract extension at PSG in 2022.

In a recent development, she was similarly crucial when Mbappe joined Real Madrid in 2024. On that occasion, she was credited for helping to secure a huge signing bonus and favourable image rights split for her son.

Fayza hasn't been afraid to publicly stand up for the forward, and she was key in the legal dispute over unpaid salary and bonuses that he felt he was owed by PSG after his exit.

PSG were ultimately ordered to pay Mbappe €60million (£52.5m) by a French court in a major victory for Fayza.

Kylian Mbappe's mum Fayza (also pictured with his brother Ethan) has played a key role in the commercial side of his career.

Sheila Ebana has been a foundational and supportive presence throughout Lamine Yamal's childhood and rise into professional football.

But, alongside regularly attending Yamal's games, Sheila has become a celebrity in her own right after embracing her public profile.

She regularly provides an insight into her life and shares behind the scenes clips with Yamal and his half brother Keyne on social media, racking up 2.8million followers on Instagram and 2.6million on TikTok.

Sheila has also regularly made paid appearances and attended VIP events, including a bizarre Christmas gala dinner that Daily Mail Sport went to in November 2025 where members of the public paid hundreds of pounds for a three-course meal, champagne, entertainment and a meet-and-greet.

To demonstrate how Sheila has embraced her fame, she once responded to online critics by retorting: 'I don't just think I'm famous - I am.'.

Lamine Yamal's mum (pictured below together with his half-brother Keyne) has embraced her celebrity fame.

Denise Bellingham – Jude Bellingham.

Jude Bellingham has often credited his mother Denise for helping to manage his life off the pitch and keep him grounded.

When he moved to Germany to join Borussia Dortmund as a 17-year-old, Denise went with him – before subsequently following the midfielder to Spain after his transfer to Real Madrid – while his father Mark stayed with his brother Jobe.

She is understood to handle his domestic affairs and finances, while Bellingham inadvertently revealed during the 2022 World Cup that she still made his bed.

Denise has generally provided a constant source of advice, logistical support – which has included driving him to training in the past – and organisational help throughout his time in the game.

The England star is clearly appreciative of all she has done, describing her as his 'queen' and 'backbone', and crediting her with helping to keep him level headed throughout the highs and lows of his career.

Jude Bellingham (pictured also with dad Mark and brother Jobe) has described his mum Denise as his 'queen' and 'backbone'.

Marcia Lewis – Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mother Marcia Lewis has played a crucial role in his rise into Arsenal and England's first team.

When Lewis-Skelly entered the Arsenal academy system at the age of eight, Marcia wanted to learn more about football to ensure she could protect and guide her son's progression.

She subsequently qualified as an agent, meaning she now represents Lewis-Skelly, and also enrolled in a Master's degree in Football Business.

Marcia has since taken part in contract negotiations and filtered external pressures away from her son during his development.

She was later inspired to set up the No1Fan.club, a platform that aims to support families who have children in academy football.

The outlet is dedicated to helping navigate various challenges that arise, such as dealing with scouts, agents and the general pressures associated with youth football.

Myles Lewis-Skelly's mum Marcia Lewis tried to learn more about the business of football so she would be able to support her son on his journey (Source: Instagram/myleslewisskelly).

Harry Maguire's mother Zoe has taken a more low-profile approach to her son's career than others, yet she has never been afraid to speak out when she feels the need to.

This included back in 2023 when she snapped after years of watching her son face significant abuse, both online and in stadiums.

At the time, Zoe labelled the heat on the defender as 'disgraceful' and 'unacceptable', and stated it went 'far beyond' football.

She re-emerged into the public eye three years later when Maguire was snubbed from England's World Cup squad.

After that, she tweeted: 'Absolutely disgusted.'.

In another post addressing Maguire, she added: 'You couldn’t have done anymore. Hold your head high …Disgraceful.'.

Sources indicate that reports now suggest an independent panel has reached a decision. If that holds up, the scale of any Chelsea Manchester City compensation payout could run into tens of millions of pounds for the Blues alone.

The Premier League charged Manchester City with 115 alleged breaches of financial regulations in February 2023. That followed a four-year investigation into the club’s accounts. The case has hung over the competition ever since. Every top-flight club knows the outcome could change how recent Premier League seasons are remembered.

This matters directly to Chelsea. If City are found to have broken spending and disclosure rules, clubs who finished below them could argue they lost out on prize money and European qualification. Chelsea have competed directly with City for top four places and cup competitions throughout that period.

It has been revealed that according to The Athletic, Manchester City were found guilty on all but one of the 115 charges by the independent panel. The Premier League has not confirmed the verdict or issued a statement.

According to recent reports, manchester City have not accepted any suggestion of guilt. The club released a statement addressing the ongoing process directly.

“The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such, Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the Club’s statement of February 2023. ‘The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence.'”.

Recent findings suggest that that statement makes clear the club does not see the case as settled. Until the Premier League confirms a result, the reported verdict will linger on for official sentencing.

It has been revealed that data specialists at OLBG have estimated the potential Chelsea Manchester City compensation windfall if City are found guilty. They believe City could owe domestic rivals well over £500m in lost Premier League prize money if the charges are proven.

It has been revealed that within that total, London clubs are said to be due around £164m between them. Chelsea, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur are among the clubs who could be entitled to a share. Other Premier League sides could benefit too, depending on where they finished compared with City in the seasons in question.

In a recent development, prize money in the Premier League is tied closely to league position. If City gained points unfairly, that would have pushed a rival down the table and cost them money too. That is the basis for the OLBG figures, and it explains why the sums involved are so large.

Sources indicate that for Chelsea, even a share of that £164m pot would be a massive boost. It could help fund fresh signings, or simply ease the pressure around the kind of transfer valuations at Stamford Bridge the club faces every window.

Sources indicate that city chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak has already made clear the case is far from finished. He described the process as having “a long way to run.” That points to appeals and further legal steps, whatever the panel has decided.

According to recent reports, chelsea, for their part, carry on with life under Xabi Alonso regardless of how the case unfolds. Attention stays on squad rotation and Xabi Alonso’s squad management strategy, not on any potential windfall. The financial case will not change anything on the pitch in the short term.

According to recent reports, the Premier League has stayed silent on the reported verdict, and confidentiality remains strict around the process, according to reports from Football.London. Chelsea fans should expect a long wait before any compensation, if it comes at all, reaches the club’s accounts.

Breaking: A grant to hand out more grants — and build a research area

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (817 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.
  • Industry observers note that amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation.
  • The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grants worth up to US$10,000 will fund niche scientific problems.Credit: SimpleImages/Getty.

Industry observers note that amid political instability and decreased funding for science worldwide, some non-profit organizations are testing whether and how microgrants — awards of US$10,000 or less — can spur innovation. The latest development comes from the Experiment Foundation, a non-profit science funding organization in Berkeley, California, which has rolled out the Field Building Accelerator to cultivate ingenuity hubs around specific fields of research using small, rapidly deployed grants.

The initiative will, in early 2027, award at least 50 individuals — called field builders — $70,000 each. The recipients, in turn, will design their own microgrant programme to distribute up to $10,000 to researchers exploring distinct facets of the same niche scientific problem. The grants will be hosted on Experiment.com, an online platform that allows organizations to advertise and fund research projects.

“We want to create a different persona in science — the people who can chart newly introduced research territory,” states David Lang, executive director of the Experiment Foundation.

Sources indicate that the accelerator programme is open to proposals that broadly target oceans, climate, toxicity, future science and conservation technology, claims Lang — reflecting the interests of its funders, including non-profit organizations such as the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation in Palo Alto, California. Prospective field builders must propose a name for the field, define its core questions and challenges, and identify at least eight researchers, laboratories or communities they would consider funding.

Judges will select field builders who they think are best placed to identify overlooked talent, back unproven ideas and bring like-minded researchers together. Ideally, indicates Lang, they will reflect diverse scientific perspectives, including early-career researchers, science journalists, science-fiction authors and venture capitalists. “There are people that build momentum in scientific fields, but they are different from the ones who are getting big publications or spinning out companies,” he says.

And, in a bid to take chances on unconventional ideas, the judges will not average scores; instead, if any of the two or three judges champions an application, it moves forward.

Although some might baulk at the idea that $10,000 grants are large enough to spur new research disciplines, others say it is time to experiment with new ways to distribute research funding. “If we really want to help to seed challenging, high risk, ‘who knows what will happen’ ideas, then small-scale grants are a good strategy,” says Brian Nosek, executive director of the Center for Open Science, a non-profit organization in Charlottesville, Virginia, that promotes transparent and reproducible science.

In a recent development, in 2025, The Science Foundation in Seattle, Washington, organized public donations to award up to $10,000 to researchers who have a compelling ‘what if’ basic-science proposal in the areas of mathematics, physical sciences and biological sciences. The foundation announced the second round of winners on 12 November.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03689-6.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
  • Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute.
  • Sources indicate that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United have conceded more goals than any other club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues this season, underlining the scale of the challenge facing Mauricio Pochettino following Sunday’s 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.

Pochettino’s first match in charge ended in a heavy defeat at Anfield after defender Leny Yoro was sent off in the eighth minute. Although the dismissal left United facing an uphill struggle, their defensive record suggests the new head coach has inherited problems that extend well beyond one match.

Sources indicate that according to an analysis published by the Premier League, United have conceded 34 goals in 16 matches across all competitions this season. That is the highest total of any club in Europe’s five major domestic leagues, with Sunday’s defeat adding four more goals to an already concerning record.

The Premier League also calculated Liverpool’s expected goals at 4.38, suggesting the hosts created enough chances to have won by an even greater margin. United’s difficulties began when Matthijs de Ligt misjudged a long ball, and Yoro fouled Alexander Isak as the Liverpool forward attempted to break through on goal.

Dominik Szoboszlai scored from the resulting free-kick, with Florian Wirtz doubling Liverpool’s advantage just three minutes later. Rio Ngumoha and substitute Victor Munoz completed the scoring after half-time.

According to recent reports, the defeat left United 19th in the Premier League, with just eight points from their opening 11 matches and one league victory all season. Pochettino acknowledged the painful nature of the result but argued that the early dismissal had transformed the contest. He also questioned whether Yoro should have been sent off, given the circumstances of the challenge on Isak.

The Argentine’s first tactical proposal was disrupted almost immediately, making it difficult to draw firm conclusions about how United might perform under him with a full complement of players.

Sources indicate that nevertheless, the defensive record accumulated before his arrival makes clear that improving the team’s organisation will be a central part of his work. The Premier League’s analysis highlighted De Ligt’s mistake before the sending-off and the opportunities Liverpool continued to create against United’s depleted defence.

United return to Champions League action on Wednesday when they travel to Portugal to face Sporting, giving Pochettino little time to address the challenges exposed at Anfield. The fixture offers an early opportunity to assess how he intends to organise his defence and whether the team can respond to another damaging result.

Pochettino must also decide how to balance defensive stability with the need to improve results. United’s league position means they cannot afford to spend too long finding that balance. The circumstances of Sunday’s defeat were unusual, and the red card undoubtedly made United’s task more difficult. But conceding 34 goals in 16 matches points to a wider problem that will require sustained improvement rather than a reaction to one result.

Sources indicate that for Pochettino, making United harder to beat is an obvious starting point. Wednesday’s trip to Sporting will provide his next opportunity to begin that process.

England’s statement on the squad changes, detailed in a report from Football.London, confirmed the wider fallout from the fixture.

“Mukasa’s call-up follows the withdrawal of Chelsea’s Jamie Gittens and Norwich City pair Kellen Fisher and Ben Chrisene through injury,” the statement read. West Ham midfielder Divine Mukasa has been called up as cover for all three.

Industry observers note that gittens has been an unused substitute in every Premier League fixture Chelsea have played this season, with his only two appearances under Xabi Alonso coming in the Carabao Cup. Those minutes have offered him little platform after his major summer move.

In a recent development, alonso’s squad selection has been a talking point since he took charge. Our earlier look at Xabi Alonso’s squad choices at Stamford Bridge covered how competitive things have become. An ankle injury will not change his pecking order in the short term. It does, though, remove any chance of him pushing his case this week.

Chelsea’s break has brought other headlines too. Cole Palmer also withdrew, for entirely different reasons, after his recall by senior boss Thomas Tuchel to the full England squad. Chelsea will be watching both returns closely before domestic football resumes.

Sources indicate that chelsea have not yet issued a formal update on the severity of the injury. Any recovery timeline will depend on an assessment by the club’s medical team once Gittens is back at Cobham. Nothing beyond the crutches seen at Molineux has been confirmed.

According to recent reports, given his limited game time this season, the immediate concern is less about missed fixtures than a setback to his integration under Alonso. Fans can follow how the squad shapes up before the next fixtures through our recent line-up updates. Further news on Gittens is expected once Chelsea’s medical staff finish their evaluation.
